## PR Description

Closes #998
### Root Cause
A placeholder check-run in `in_progress` whose owning workflow run terminated had no close path for four of the five cycle outcomes: the gh-857 in-place conclusion only mirrors a **green** verdict (and only with a probed green cover, no active head run, and an app token). Failure/superseded/cancelled/died cycles and all pre-fix leaks left the zombie pinned to its SHA — mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED forever (live fa #1563, head `f3d58647`, check-run 117469671401), and the legacy same-sha re-dispatch cannot conclude a stamp nothing will conclude.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — gh-998 lifecycle contract: `CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` + `conclusionForOutcome` (capability table), `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle` (AC1 state machine over the five outcomes; unknown outcome fails safe, double-close rejected — E1 idempotence), `zombieSweptLine` (I5 log format).
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-998 neutral sweep in the validate-pr placeholder/orphan block: terminal-owner orphans (gh-865 detector) whose cycle left no verdict are force-completed as `neutral` under the cycle's own app token (I3/I4), with the gh-857 AC2 fail-safes unchanged (no active head run; green-probe corner falls through untouched). New transport `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` emits `zombie-swept: <id> head <sha>` per close; rejections retry next tick (E2). Per-tick counter reset in `action()`.
- `js/factoryState.js` — cumulative `zombiesSwept` rides the state snapshot (I5); smAgent passes the tick count at the `buildFactoryState` call site.
- Link-less placeholders deliberately keep the gh-852 fresh-sha reset (a same-sha re-dispatch re-mints them — only a fresh head cures that pathology, gh-852 AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — 8 new tests: conclusion mapping, five-outcome lifecycle (incl. 3-placeholder multi-item), fail-safe unknown outcome, idempotent double-close rejection, `zombie-swept` log line. RED first (8 failed), GREEN after implementation.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 4 new tests: stable-shape 0, tick count, cumulative carry, malformed-carry restart.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **3590 passed, 0 failed** (clean-env re-run: 3538 passed, 0 failed — delta is env-dependent skips; new suites pass 49/49 and 145/145 standalone).

### Notes
- The creation-side finally-path for the kicker stub (Q1, shared helper) and the E2E/REG sandbox scenarios (AC4/AC5) live in the factory/kicker repos and CI — out of this repo's reach; this change is the SM-side finally-path + sweper (Q2 per-tick piggyback) + observability.
- A `neutral` close is honest but not a green verdict: the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered (I3).

# gh-998: Zombie in_progress check-run survives head change and blocks merge forever (fa #1563 live)

## Description

## Goal — leaked placeholder check-runs become unreachable, and existing zombies get swept (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **a check-run in state `in_progress`/`queued` whose owning workflow run has already terminated becomes unreachable state** — every cycle that opens placeholder check-runs closes them in a finally-path, every superseded cycle force-completes its leftovers, and a sweeper heals check-runs leaked before this fix.

Today the kicker registers long-lived placeholder check-runs (e.g. `Quality gate`, `JS engine integration`, `Binaries smoke gate`) on a fresh head so the PR shows "under validation" while the real gate is a dispatch-only workflow; when the cycle is superseded (new head, re-dispatch, cancellation) or ends, the placeholders are not closed. A leaked `in_progress` check is pinned to its SHA forever: GitHub computes the required-check state per name across ALL suites on the head, so ONE zombie `Quality gate` holds `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even when 58 sibling checks are green and a genuine `Quality gate: success` exists from the real CI run. The merge bot then waits `checks=pending` every tick and the PR cannot merge by any machine action — the branch is not behind, so no re-validation cycle helps.

Live instance 2026-10-17 (fa #1563, head `f3d58647`): suite 105847141092 created by the kicker push at 18:15:41Z; placeholder `Quality gate` registered 18:24:18Z (check-run id 117469671401) stayed `in_progress` 40+ minutes past its cycle; PR hard-stuck at BLOCKED; operator could not close it via REST (`POST /check-runs/{id}/completed` → 404: only the creating app may complete its own check-runs). The PR only escaped because it merged by other means. Closing that escape hatch is what makes this card load-bearing.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "close zombie check-runs by hand via API when found." Impossible in practice (creator-only restriction) and wrong in principle (see owner directive on dmtools-agents#994: manual cleanup masks the bug; the pipeline must not depend on humans GC-ing its leaks).
- **Retracted:** "the merge bot should treat in_progress checks whose workflow run completed as stale." That is the *detection* half and survives only as an input to the sweeper; the *cure* must be closing the leak at creation time plus healing what already leaked.
- **Retracted:** "wait for the next head — zombies die with their SHA." True only while the head keeps moving; a green, up-to-date, fully-validated PR with a zombie on its CURRENT head (the live instance) has no reason to move. A system where the only cure is generating new work is a leak with extra steps.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle (subject of every verb is the **check-run object**, owned by a **validation cycle** keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
cycle start (kicker/rework/operator push → new head H)
   │ registers placeholders P1..Pn on H via Checks API
   ▼
validation dispatched (dispatch-only CI, separate workflow)
   │ outcomes: success | failure | superseded (new head H') | cancelled
   ▼
finally-path [THE FIX — runs for EVERY outcome]
   ├── close P1..Pn on H with the cycle's real conclusion
   │      (success→success, failure→failure, superseded→neutral)
   └── force-complete any P_i still queued/in_progress even if the
       closing call itself failed (retry w/ backoff, then escalate)
        │
        ▼
[sweeper — self-heal pre-fix leaks]
   scan heads of open, non-dirty PRs for check-runs where
   status ∈ {queued, in_progress} AND owning workflow_run is in
   a terminal state → force-complete as neutral + log `zombie-swept`
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — leak-free creation:** for every placeholder P registered by a cycle, the cycle's termination (any path, including process kill between register and dispatch) results in P being terminal within one SM tick. There is no code path that leaves P open.
- **I2 — detection is grounded, not heuristic:** the sweeper never force-completes a check-run whose owning workflow run is still live. A live `in_progress` `Quality gate` is legitimate; only terminal-owner + open-check is a zombie.
- **I3 — required-check semantics preserved:** placeholder conclusions always mirror the cycle's real outcome (never a blanket `success`), so GitHub's required-check verdict stays truthful. `neutral` is reserved for superseded cycles — a superseded cycle carries no verdict about its head.
- **I4 — creator-only boundary respected:** all close operations run under the same app identity that created the check-runs (the cycle's own token); no cross-app completion is attempted, because GitHub rejects it (404) by design.
- **I5 — observability:** every close and every sweep action leaves a machine-log line (`check-close: <run-id> <conclusion>` / `zombie-swept: <check-run-id> head <sha>`); zombies found by the sweeper are counted in the factory state payload so operators see the leak rate, not just the fix.

## Capability surface (every cycle outcome → close obligation)

| Cycle outcome | Placeholders closed today? | Must close (this card) | Conclusion value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation success | NO (live instance: success run, open placeholder) | YES — core | `success` |
| Validation failure | unknown, assumed NO (same path) | YES — core | `failure` (keeps the PR honestly parked) |
| Superseded by newer head H' | NO | YES — core | `neutral` (no verdict carried across heads) |
| Cycle cancelled (dup dispatch, timeout) | NO | YES — core | `neutral` |
| Process died between register and dispatch | NO | YES — core (recovered by finally-on-next-tick) | `neutral` |
| Pre-fix leaked zombies on existing PRs | n/a | YES — sweeper, second tier | `neutral` + count metric |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I5 for all rows above; the finally-path lives in the SAME job that registers placeholders, so it inherits the creator token (I4 for free).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** the sweeper generalizes to a periodic (hourly) repo-wide scan for terminal-owner open checks on ANY ref, plus a factory-state metric page for the leak counter.
- **Excluded (rationale):** completing OTHER apps' check-runs (GitHub forbids; listed as *impossible*, not excluded-by-taste); changing the required-check configuration (repo settings are out of scope); converting placeholders to real job-based checks (a larger redesign — follow-up card if desired).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: the placeholder-lifecycle state machine transitions register→(success|failure|superseded|cancelled|died)→closed with the correct conclusion per the table; no transition leaves the object open. *Hook: pure state-machine UT over the five outcomes.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub API): a scripted cycle that registers 3 placeholders, then terminates with each of the five outcomes → each placeholder receives exactly one close call with the mapped conclusion; a kill between register and dispatch is recovered by the next tick's finally. *Hook: scripted API fixture with call assertions.*
- **AC3** — Zombie detection: given a check-run with `status=in_progress` whose `check_suite`/`workflow_run` is terminal, the sweeper force-completes it as `neutral` and emits the `zombie-swept` log line; a live-owner `in_progress` check is never touched. *Hook: IT with two fixtures (terminal owner vs live owner).*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox repo): reproduce the fa #1563 shape — kicker push → placeholders → superseding push → real CI green on the final head → PR mergeable WITHOUT any human or sweeper intervention, because no zombie exists on the final head. *Hook: E2E scenario named `zombie-repro-1563`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded fa #1563 timeline (suite 105847141092, check-run 117469671401) against the sweeper → the check-run ends terminal as `neutral`, the metric increments, and the PR's computed mergeability flips to the real (green) verdict. *Hook: REG fixture from the live incident; CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green…

This is the same exposure gh-865's conclude has (pre-existing), but the new sweep runs in a strictly broader trigger condition (previously the whole block required green probe; now any non-green head with orphans triggers PATCH attempts). However: gh-865's in-place conclude already had this exposure in the green case. The neutral sweep broadens it to every red/no-verdict head. Still, real-world check-runs with linked workflow runs are usually GitHub Actions ones; third-party check runs typically don't have a workflow_run link, so runIdOf would be null and they'd be excluded. So the risk is moderate-low. Could flag as SUGESTION (filter to own-app or mark-and-skip persistent rejections).

2. **Behavioral gating concern — the gh-857 gate widening.** Previously: `if (vProbe && vProbe.green && silentToken)`. Now: `if (silentToken)` and inside, phCover is only probed when probe is green. Per gh-998's capability table, a `failure` outcome should close placeholders as `failure` — closing as `neutral` when the cycle actually failed... Hmm, wait: if the probe is red, the head HAS a real failure verdict (from the dispatched run). The placeholder zombie is a leak; the required check truth is carried by the red stamp. Neutral for the zombie is fine and arguably the sweper can't do better (it can't re-run the cycle to mint a failure conclusion under the placeholder). Also neutral doesn't unblock a required check gate (neutral typically doesn't satisfy required checks) — the PR stays parked honestly. So no laundering. OK.

3. **A more significant correctness question**: the sweep fires when `vProbe` is missing/null entirely. What is vProbe? Let me check — it's probably the probe of the validation verdict. If vProbe is null because the probe FAILED (couldn't determine), the sweep concludes orphans as neutral even though a green verdict may exist — but wait, if probe failed, gh-857 previously did nothing too (gate required vProbe.green). Neutral close is honest regardless. And the green cover probe (`greenCoverRun`) is only skipped when probe is not green — but greenCoverRun probes workflow runs directly, independent of vProbe. Actually branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head) — a neutral conclusion now becomes the latest stamp for that check-run... but it's the same check-run object; the real CI green verdict lives in a DIFFERENT check-run (dispatched run's own check). After neutral close, does the required check resolve to success (latest conclusion?) or neutral? GitHub required check evaluation: for a check run, the latest execution matters? Actually each check-run is per suite; the required status check looks across check-runs by name — GitHub docs: if multiple check runs with the same name, the most recent one (by creation?) is used. The PR description says "a pending required check counts per name across ALL suites on the head". The PR notes acknowledge "the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered". Whether neutral + success = mergeable is GitHub behavior; the PR claims live validation. Can't verify here. Fine.

4. **E2 escalation gap**: ticket E2 says "a persistent failure escalates to an issue (existing alarm path) rather than silently leaking — degradation path". - **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:26:39Z

## PR Description

Closes #998
### Root Cause
A placeholder check-run in `in_progress` whose owning workflow run terminated had no close path for four of the five cycle outcomes: the gh-857 in-place conclusion only mirrors a **green** verdict (and only with a probed green cover, no active head run, and an app token). Failure/superseded/cancelled/died cycles and all pre-fix leaks left the zombie pinned to its SHA — mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED forever (live fa #1563, head `f3d58647`, check-run 117469671401), and the legacy same-sha re-dispatch cannot conclude a stamp nothing will conclude.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — gh-998 lifecycle contract: `CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` + `conclusionForOutcome` (capability table), `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle` (AC1 state machine over the five outcomes; unknown outcome fails safe, double-close rejected — E1 idempotence), `zombieSweptLine` (I5 log format).
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-998 neutral sweep in the validate-pr placeholder/orphan block: terminal-owner orphans (gh-865 detector) whose cycle left no verdict are force-completed as `neutral` under the cycle's own app token (I3/I4), with the gh-857 AC2 fail-safes unchanged (no active head run; green-probe corner falls through untouched). New transport `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` emits `zombie-swept: <id> head <sha>` per close; rejections retry next tick (E2). Per-tick counter reset in `action()`.
- `js/factoryState.js` — cumulative `zombiesSwept` rides the state snapshot (I5); smAgent passes the tick count at the `buildFactoryState` call site.
- Link-less placeholders deliberately keep the gh-852 fresh-sha reset (a same-sha re-dispatch re-mints them — only a fresh head cures that pathology, gh-852 AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — 8 new tests: conclusion mapping, five-outcome lifecycle (incl. 3-placeholder multi-item), fail-safe unknown outcome, idempotent double-close rejection, `zombie-swept` log line. RED first (8 failed), GREEN after implementation.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 4 new tests: stable-shape 0, tick count, cumulative carry, malformed-carry restart.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **3590 passed, 0 failed** (clean-env re-run: 3538 passed, 0 failed — delta is env-dependent skips; new suites pass 49/49 and 145/145 standalone).

### Notes
- The creation-side finally-path for the kicker stub (Q1, shared helper) and the E2E/REG sandbox scenarios (AC4/AC5) live in the factory/kicker repos and CI — out of this repo's reach; this change is the SM-side finally-path + sweper (Q2 per-tick piggyback) + observability.
- A `neutral` close is honest but not a green verdict: the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered (I3).

blocks.text:
# gh-998: Zombie in_progress check-run survives head change and blocks merge forever (fa #1563 live)

## Description

## Goal — leaked placeholder check-runs become unreachable, and existing zombies get swept (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **a check-run in state `in_progress`/`queued` whose owning workflow run has already terminated becomes unreachable state** — every cycle that opens placeholder check-runs closes them in a finally-path, every superseded cycle force-completes its leftovers, and a sweeper heals check-runs leaked before this fix.

Today the kicker registers long-lived placeholder check-runs (e.g. `Quality gate`, `JS engine integration`, `Binaries smoke gate`) on a fresh head so the PR shows "under validation" while the real gate is a dispatch-only workflow; when the cycle is superseded (new head, re-dispatch, cancellation) or ends, the placeholders are not closed. A leaked `in_progress` check is pinned to its SHA forever: GitHub computes the required-check state per name across ALL suites on the head, so ONE zombie `Quality gate` holds `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even when 58 sibling checks are green and a genuine `Quality gate: success` exists from the real CI run. The merge bot then waits `checks=pending` every tick and the PR cannot merge by any machine action — the branch is not behind, so no re-validation cycle helps.

Live instance 2026-10-17 (fa #1563, head `f3d58647`): suite 105847141092 created by the kicker push at 18:15:41Z; placeholder `Quality gate` registered 18:24:18Z (check-run id 117469671401) stayed `in_progress` 40+ minutes past its cycle; PR hard-stuck at BLOCKED; operator could not close it via REST (`POST /check-runs/{id}/completed` → 404: only the creating app may complete its own check-runs). The PR only escaped because it merged by other means. Closing that escape hatch is what makes this card load-bearing.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "close zombie check-runs by hand via API when found." Impossible in practice (creator-only restriction) and wrong in principle (see owner directive on dmtools-agents#994: manual cleanup masks the bug; the pipeline must not depend on humans GC-ing its leaks).
- **Retracted:** "the merge bot should treat in_progress checks whose workflow run completed as stale." That is the *detection* half and survives only as an input to the sweeper; the *cure* must be closing the leak at creation time plus healing what already leaked.
- **Retracted:** "wait for the next head — zombies die with their SHA." True only while the head keeps moving; a green, up-to-date, fully-validated PR with a zombie on its CURRENT head (the live instance) has no reason to move. A system where the only cure is generating new work is a leak with extra steps.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle (subject of every verb is the **check-run object**, owned by a **validation cycle** keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
cycle start (kicker/rework/operator push → new head H)
   │ registers placeholders P1..Pn on H via Checks API
   ▼
validation dispatched (dispatch-only CI, separate workflow)
   │ outcomes: success | failure | superseded (new head H') | cancelled
   ▼
finally-path [THE FIX — runs for EVERY outcome]
   ├── close P1..Pn on H with the cycle's real conclusion
   │      (success→success, failure→failure, superseded→neutral)
   └── force-complete any P_i still queued/in_progress even if the
       closing call itself failed (retry w/ backoff, then escalate)
        │
        ▼
[sweeper — self-heal pre-fix leaks]
   scan heads of open, non-dirty PRs for check-runs where
   status ∈ {queued, in_progress} AND owning workflow_run is in
   a terminal state → force-complete as neutral + log `zombie-swept`
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — leak-free creation:** for every placeholder P registered by a cycle, the cycle's termination (any path, including process kill between register and dispatch) results in P being terminal within one SM tick. There is no code path that leaves P open.
- **I2 — detection is grounded, not heuristic:** the sweeper never force-completes a check-run whose owning workflow run is still live. A live `in_progress` `Quality gate` is legitimate; only terminal-owner + open-check is a zombie.
- **I3 — required-check semantics preserved:** placeholder conclusions always mirror the cycle's real outcome (never a blanket `success`), so GitHub's required-check verdict stays truthful. `neutral` is reserved for superseded cycles — a superseded cycle carries no verdict about its head.
- **I4 — creator-only boundary respected:** all close operations run under the same app identity that created the check-runs (the cycle's own token); no cross-app completion is attempted, because GitHub rejects it (404) by design.
- **I5 — observability:** every close and every sweep action leaves a machine-log line (`check-close: <run-id> <conclusion>` / `zombie-swept: <check-run-id> head <sha>`); zombies found by the sweeper are counted in the factory state payload so operators see the leak rate, not just the fix.

## Capability surface (every cycle outcome → close obligation)

| Cycle outcome | Placeholders closed today? | Must close (this card) | Conclusion value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation success | NO (live instance: success run, open placeholder) | YES — core | `success` |
| Validation failure | unknown, assumed NO (same path) | YES — core | `failure` (keeps the PR honestly parked) |
| Superseded by newer head H' | NO | YES — core | `neutral` (no verdict carried across heads) |
| Cycle cancelled (dup dispatch, timeout) | NO | YES — core | `neutral` |
| Process died between register and dispatch | NO | YES — core (recovered by finally-on-next-tick) | `neutral` |
| Pre-fix leaked zombies on existing PRs | n/a | YES — sweeper, second tier | `neutral` + count metric |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I5 for all rows above; the finally-path lives in the SAME job that registers placeholders, so it inherits the creator token (I4 for free).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** the sweeper generalizes to a periodic (hourly) repo-wide scan for terminal-owner open checks on ANY ref, plus a factory-state metric page for the leak counter.
- **Excluded (rationale):** completing OTHER apps' check-runs (GitHub forbids; listed as *impossible*, not excluded-by-taste); changing the required-check configuration (repo settings are out of scope); converting placeholders to real job-based checks (a larger redesign — follow-up card if desired).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: the placeholder-lifecycle state machine transitions register→(success|failure|superseded|cancelled|died)→closed with the correct conclusion per the table; no transition leaves the object open. *Hook: pure state-machine UT over the five outcomes.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub API): a scripted cycle that registers 3 placeholders, then terminates with each of the five outcomes → each placeholder receives exactly one close call with the mapped conclusion; a kill between register and dispatch is recovered by the next tick's finally. *Hook: scripted API fixture with call assertions.*
- **AC3** — Zombie detection: given a check-run with `status=in_progress` whose `check_suite`/`workflow_run` is terminal, the sweeper force-completes it as `neutral` and emits the `zombie-swept` log line; a live-owner `in_progress` check is never touched. *Hook: IT with two fixtures (terminal owner vs live owner).*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox repo): reproduce the fa #1563 shape — kicker push → placeholders → superseding push → real CI green on the final head → PR mergeable WITHOUT any human or sweeper intervention, because no zombie exists on the final head. *Hook: E2E scenario named `zombie-repro-1563`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded fa #1563 timeline (suite 105847141092, check-run 117469671401) against the sweeper → the check-run ends terminal as `neutral`, the metric increments, and the PR's computed mergeability flips to the real (green) verdict. *Hook: REG fixture from the live incident; CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green…

For a third-party app's check-run (e.g., codecov), the PATCH will fail with 403/404 → `out.rejected` set, warns every tick, retries forever. This is the same exposure gh-865's conclude has (pre-existing), but the new sweep runs in a strictly broader trigger condition (previously the whole block required green probe; now any non-green head with orphans triggers PATCH attempts). However: gh-865's in-place conclude already had this exposure in the green case. The neutral sweep broadens it to every red/no-verdict head. - **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:26:39Z

## PR Description

Closes #998
### Root Cause
A placeholder check-run in `in_progress` whose owning workflow run terminated had no close path for four of the five cycle outcomes: the gh-857 in-place conclusion only mirrors a **green** verdict (and only with a probed green cover, no active head run, and an app token). Failure/superseded/cancelled/died cycles and all pre-fix leaks left the zombie pinned to its SHA — mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED forever (live fa #1563, head `f3d58647`, check-run 117469671401), and the legacy same-sha re-dispatch cannot conclude a stamp nothing will conclude.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — gh-998 lifecycle contract: `CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` + `conclusionForOutcome` (capability table), `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle` (AC1 state machine over the five outcomes; unknown outcome fails safe, double-close rejected — E1 idempotence), `zombieSweptLine` (I5 log format).
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-998 neutral sweep in the validate-pr placeholder/orphan block: terminal-owner orphans (gh-865 detector) whose cycle left no verdict are force-completed as `neutral` under the cycle's own app token (I3/I4), with the gh-857 AC2 fail-safes unchanged (no active head run; green-probe corner falls through untouched). New transport `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` emits `zombie-swept: <id> head <sha>` per close; rejections retry next tick (E2). Per-tick counter reset in `action()`.
- `js/factoryState.js` — cumulative `zombiesSwept` rides the state snapshot (I5); smAgent passes the tick count at the `buildFactoryState` call site.
- Link-less placeholders deliberately keep the gh-852 fresh-sha reset (a same-sha re-dispatch re-mints them — only a fresh head cures that pathology, gh-852 AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — 8 new tests: conclusion mapping, five-outcome lifecycle (incl. 3-placeholder multi-item), fail-safe unknown outcome, idempotent double-close rejection, `zombie-swept` log line. RED first (8 failed), GREEN after implementation.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 4 new tests: stable-shape 0, tick count, cumulative carry, malformed-carry restart.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **3590 passed, 0 failed** (clean-env re-run: 3538 passed, 0 failed — delta is env-dependent skips; new suites pass 49/49 and 145/145 standalone).

### Notes
- The creation-side finally-path for the kicker stub (Q1, shared helper) and the E2E/REG sandbox scenarios (AC4/AC5) live in the factory/kicker repos and CI — out of this repo's reach; this change is the SM-side finally-path + sweper (Q2 per-tick piggyback) + observability.
- A `neutral` close is honest but not a green verdict: the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered (I3).

# gh-998: Zombie in_progress check-run survives head change and blocks merge forever (fa #1563 live)

## Description

## Goal — leaked placeholder check-runs become unreachable, and existing zombies get swept (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **a check-run in state `in_progress`/`queued` whose owning workflow run has already terminated becomes unreachable state** — every cycle that opens placeholder check-runs closes them in a finally-path, every superseded cycle force-completes its leftovers, and a sweeper heals check-runs leaked before this fix.

Today the kicker registers long-lived placeholder check-runs (e.g. `Quality gate`, `JS engine integration`, `Binaries smoke gate`) on a fresh head so the PR shows "under validation" while the real gate is a dispatch-only workflow; when the cycle is superseded (new head, re-dispatch, cancellation) or ends, the placeholders are not closed. A leaked `in_progress` check is pinned to its SHA forever: GitHub computes the required-check state per name across ALL suites on the head, so ONE zombie `Quality gate` holds `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even when 58 sibling checks are green and a genuine `Quality gate: success` exists from the real CI run. The merge bot then waits `checks=pending` every tick and the PR cannot merge by any machine action — the branch is not behind, so no re-validation cycle helps.

Live instance 2026-10-17 (fa #1563, head `f3d58647`): suite 105847141092 created by the kicker push at 18:15:41Z; placeholder `Quality gate` registered 18:24:18Z (check-run id 117469671401) stayed `in_progress` 40+ minutes past its cycle; PR hard-stuck at BLOCKED; operator could not close it via REST (`POST /check-runs/{id}/completed` → 404: only the creating app may complete its own check-runs). The PR only escaped because it merged by other means. Closing that escape hatch is what makes this card load-bearing.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "close zombie check-runs by hand via API when found." Impossible in practice (creator-only restriction) and wrong in principle (see owner directive on dmtools-agents#994: manual cleanup masks the bug; the pipeline must not depend on humans GC-ing its leaks).
- **Retracted:** "the merge bot should treat in_progress checks whose workflow run completed as stale." That is the *detection* half and survives only as an input to the sweeper; the *cure* must be closing the leak at creation time plus healing what already leaked.
- **Retracted:** "wait for the next head — zombies die with their SHA." True only while the head keeps moving; a green, up-to-date, fully-validated PR with a zombie on its CURRENT head (the live instance) has no reason to move. A system where the only cure is generating new work is a leak with extra steps.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle (subject of every verb is the **check-run object**, owned by a **validation cycle** keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
cycle start (kicker/rework/operator push → new head H)
   │ registers placeholders P1..Pn on H via Checks API
   ▼
validation dispatched (dispatch-only CI, separate workflow)
   │ outcomes: success | failure | superseded (new head H') | cancelled
   ▼
finally-path [THE FIX — runs for EVERY outcome]
   ├── close P1..Pn on H with the cycle's real conclusion
   │      (success→success, failure→failure, superseded→neutral)
   └── force-complete any P_i still queued/in_progress even if the
       closing call itself failed (retry w/ backoff, then escalate)
        │
        ▼
[sweeper — self-heal pre-fix leaks]
   scan heads of open, non-dirty PRs for check-runs where
   status ∈ {queued, in_progress} AND owning workflow_run is in
   a terminal state → force-complete as neutral + log `zombie-swept`
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — leak-free creation:** for every placeholder P registered by a cycle, the cycle's termination (any path, including process kill between register and dispatch) results in P being terminal within one SM tick. There is no code path that leaves P open.
- **I2 — detection is grounded, not heuristic:** the sweeper never force-completes a check-run whose owning workflow run is still live. A live `in_progress` `Quality gate` is legitimate; only terminal-owner + open-check is a zombie.
- **I3 — required-check semantics preserved:** placeholder conclusions always mirror the cycle's real outcome (never a blanket `success`), so GitHub's required-check verdict stays truthful. `neutral` is reserved for superseded cycles — a superseded cycle carries no verdict about its head.
- **I4 — creator-only boundary respected:** all close operations run under the same app identity that created the check-runs (the cycle's own token); no cross-app completion is attempted, because GitHub rejects it (404) by design.
- **I5 — observability:** every close and every sweep action leaves a machine-log line (`check-close: <run-id> <conclusion>` / `zombie-swept: <check-run-id> head <sha>`); zombies found by the sweeper are counted in the factory state payload so operators see the leak rate, not just the fix.

## Capability surface (every cycle outcome → close obligation)

| Cycle outcome | Placeholders closed today? | Must close (this card) | Conclusion value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation success | NO (live instance: success run, open placeholder) | YES — core | `success` |
| Validation failure | unknown, assumed NO (same path) | YES — core | `failure` (keeps the PR honestly parked) |
| Superseded by newer head H' | NO | YES — core | `neutral` (no verdict carried across heads) |
| Cycle cancelled (dup dispatch, timeout) | NO | YES — core | `neutral` |
| Process died between register and dispatch | NO | YES — core (recovered by finally-on-next-tick) | `neutral` |
| Pre-fix leaked zombies on existing PRs | n/a | YES — sweeper, second tier | `neutral` + count metric |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I5 for all rows above; the finally-path lives in the SAME job that registers placeholders, so it inherits the creator token (I4 for free).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** the sweeper generalizes to a periodic (hourly) repo-wide scan for terminal-owner open checks on ANY ref, plus a factory-state metric page for the leak counter.
- **Excluded (rationale):** completing OTHER apps' check-runs (GitHub forbids; listed as *impossible*, not excluded-by-taste); changing the required-check configuration (repo settings are out of scope); converting placeholders to real job-based checks (a larger redesign — follow-up card if desired).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: the placeholder-lifecycle state machine transitions register→(success|failure|superseded|cancelled|died)→closed with the correct conclusion per the table; no transition leaves the object open. *Hook: pure state-machine UT over the five outcomes.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub API): a scripted cycle that registers 3 placeholders, then terminates with each of the five outcomes → each placeholder receives exactly one close call with the mapped conclusion; a kill between register and dispatch is recovered by the next tick's finally. *Hook: scripted API fixture with call assertions.*
- **AC3** — Zombie detection: given a check-run with `status=in_progress` whose `check_suite`/`workflow_run` is terminal, the sweeper force-completes it as `neutral` and emits the `zombie-swept` log line; a live-owner `in_progress` check is never touched. *Hook: IT with two fixtures (terminal owner vs live owner).*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox repo): reproduce the fa #1563 shape — kicker push → placeholders → superseding push → real CI green on the final head → PR mergeable WITHOUT any human or sweeper intervention, because no zombie exists on the final head. *Hook: E2E scenario named `zombie-repro-1563`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded fa #1563 timeline (suite 105847141092, check-run 117469671401) against the sweeper → the check-run ends terminal as `neutral`, the metric increments, and the PR's computed mergeability flips to the real (green) verdict. *Hook: REG fixture from the live incident; CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green…

Key observations so far:

1. **The sweep target set** (`vOrphans` via `orphanedRunChecks`) is NOT filtered to the github-actions App's own check-runs — it includes ANY pending check-run with a terminal owning run. For a third-party app's check-run (e.g., codecov), the PATCH will fail with 403/404 → `out.rejected` set, warns every tick, retries forever. This is the same exposure gh-865's conclude has (pre-existing), but the new sweep runs in a strictly broader trigger condition (previously the whole block required green probe; now any non-green head with orphans triggers PATCH attempts). However: gh-865's in-place conclude already had this exposure in the green case. The neutral sweep broadens it to every red/no-verdict head. Still, real-world check-runs with linked workflow runs are usually GitHub Actions ones; third-party check runs typically don't have a workflow_run link, so runIdOf would be null and they'd be excluded. So the risk is moderate-low. Could flag as SUGESTION (filter to own-app or mark-and-skip persistent rejections).

2. **Behavioral gating concern — the gh-857 gate widening.** Previously: `if (vProbe && vProbe.green && silentToken)`. Now: `if (silentToken)` and inside, phCover is only probed when probe is green. Neutral sweep condition: `vOrphans.length && !(vProbe && vProbe.green)`. So when the probe is RED (validation genuinely failed on this head), the sweep force-completes orphan placeholders as neutral. Per gh-998's capability table, a `failure` outcome should close placeholders as `failure` — closing as `neutral` when the cycle actually failed... Hmm, wait: if the probe is red, the head HAS a real failure verdict (from the dispatched run). The placeholder zombie is a leak; the required check truth is carried by the red stamp. Neutral for the zombie is fine and arguably the sweper can't do better (it can't re-run the cycle to mint a failure conclusion under the placeholder). Also neutral doesn't unblock a required check gate (neutral typically doesn't satisfy required checks) — the PR stays parked honestly. So no laundering. OK.

3. **A more significant correctness question**: the sweep fires when `vProbe` is missing/null entirely. What is vProbe? Let me check — it's probably the probe of the validation verdict. If vProbe is null because the probe FAILED (couldn't determine), the sweep concludes orphans as neutral even though a green verdict may exist — but wait, if probe failed, gh-857 previously did nothing too (gate required vProbe.green). Closing a zombie as neutral when the head actually has a green verdict in flight... the orphan detector requires the OWNING run to be terminal past grace, so the check-run genuinely is orphaned. Neutral close is honest regardless. And the green cover probe (`greenCoverRun`) is only skipped when probe is not green — but greenCoverRun probes workflow runs directly, independent of vProbe. If vProbe is null (probe error) but a real green cover exists, the sweep closes orphans neutral instead of success-mirroring — mildly suboptimal but not a correctness bug (the genuine green stamp from real CI still exists separately; the neutral placeholder won't override the latest-per-name? ## PR Description

Closes #998
### Root Cause
A placeholder check-run in `in_progress` whose owning workflow run terminated had no close path for four of the five cycle outcomes: the gh-857 in-place conclusion only mirrors a **green** verdict (and only with a probed green cover, no active head run, and an app token). Failure/superseded/cancelled/died cycles and all pre-fix leaks left the zombie pinned to its SHA — mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED forever (live fa #1563, head `f3d58647`, check-run 117469671401), and the legacy same-sha re-dispatch cannot conclude a stamp nothing will conclude.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — gh-998 lifecycle contract: `CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` + `conclusionForOutcome` (capability table), `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle` (AC1 state machine over the five outcomes; unknown outcome fails safe, double-close rejected — E1 idempotence), `zombieSweptLine` (I5 log format).
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-998 neutral sweep in the validate-pr placeholder/orphan block: terminal-owner orphans (gh-865 detector) whose cycle left no verdict are force-completed as `neutral` under the cycle's own app token (I3/I4), with the gh-857 AC2 fail-safes unchanged (no active head run; green-probe corner falls through untouched). New transport `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` emits `zombie-swept: <id> head <sha>` per close; rejections retry next tick (E2). Per-tick counter reset in `action()`.
- `js/factoryState.js` — cumulative `zombiesSwept` rides the state snapshot (I5); smAgent passes the tick count at the `buildFactoryState` call site.
- Link-less placeholders deliberately keep the gh-852 fresh-sha reset (a same-sha re-dispatch re-mints them — only a fresh head cures that pathology, gh-852 AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — 8 new tests: conclusion mapping, five-outcome lifecycle (incl. 3-placeholder multi-item), fail-safe unknown outcome, idempotent double-close rejection, `zombie-swept` log line. RED first (8 failed), GREEN after implementation.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 4 new tests: stable-shape 0, tick count, cumulative carry, malformed-carry restart.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **3590 passed, 0 failed** (clean-env re-run: 3538 passed, 0 failed — delta is env-dependent skips; new suites pass 49/49 and 145/145 standalone).

### Notes
- The creation-side finally-path for the kicker stub (Q1, shared helper) and the E2E/REG sandbox scenarios (AC4/AC5) live in the factory/kicker repos and CI — out of this repo's reach; this change is the SM-side finally-path + sweper (Q2 per-tick piggyback) + observability.
- A `neutral` close is honest but not a green verdict: the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered (I3).

blocks.text:
# gh-998: Zombie in_progress check-run survives head change and blocks merge forever (fa #1563 live)

## Description

## Goal — leaked placeholder check-runs become unreachable, and existing zombies get swept (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **a check-run in state `in_progress`/`queued` whose owning workflow run has already terminated becomes unreachable state** — every cycle that opens placeholder check-runs closes them in a finally-path, every superseded cycle force-completes its leftovers, and a sweeper heals check-runs leaked before this fix.

Today the kicker registers long-lived placeholder check-runs (e.g. `Quality gate`, `JS engine integration`, `Binaries smoke gate`) on a fresh head so the PR shows "under validation" while the real gate is a dispatch-only workflow; when the cycle is superseded (new head, re-dispatch, cancellation) or ends, the placeholders are not closed. A leaked `in_progress` check is pinned to its SHA forever: GitHub computes the required-check state per name across ALL suites on the head, so ONE zombie `Quality gate` holds `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even when 58 sibling checks are green and a genuine `Quality gate: success` exists from the real CI run. The merge bot then waits `checks=pending` every tick and the PR cannot merge by any machine action — the branch is not behind, so no re-validation cycle helps.

Live instance 2026-10-17 (fa #1563, head `f3d58647`): suite 105847141092 created by the kicker push at 18:15:41Z; placeholder `Quality gate` registered 18:24:18Z (check-run id 117469671401) stayed `in_progress` 40+ minutes past its cycle; PR hard-stuck at BLOCKED; operator could not close it via REST (`POST /check-runs/{id}/completed` → 404: only the creating app may complete its own check-runs). The PR only escaped because it merged by other means. Closing that escape hatch is what makes this card load-bearing.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "close zombie check-runs by hand via API when found." Impossible in practice (creator-only restriction) and wrong in principle (see owner directive on dmtools-agents#994: manual cleanup masks the bug; the pipeline must not depend on humans GC-ing its leaks).
- **Retracted:** "the merge bot should treat in_progress checks whose workflow run completed as stale." That is the *detection* half and survives only as an input to the sweeper; the *cure* must be closing the leak at creation time plus healing what already leaked.
- **Retracted:** "wait for the next head — zombies die with their SHA." True only while the head keeps moving; a green, up-to-date, fully-validated PR with a zombie on its CURRENT head (the live instance) has no reason to move. A system where the only cure is generating new work is a leak with extra steps.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle (subject of every verb is the **check-run object**, owned by a **validation cycle** keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
cycle start (kicker/rework/operator push → new head H)
   │ registers placeholders P1..Pn on H via Checks API
   ▼
validation dispatched (dispatch-only CI, separate workflow)
   │ outcomes: success | failure | superseded (new head H') | cancelled
   ▼
finally-path [THE FIX — runs for EVERY outcome]
   ├── close P1..Pn on H with the cycle's real conclusion
   │      (success→success, failure→failure, superseded→neutral)
   └── force-complete any P_i still queued/in_progress even if the
       closing call itself failed (retry w/ backoff, then escalate)
        │
        ▼
[sweeper — self-heal pre-fix leaks]
   scan heads of open, non-dirty PRs for check-runs where
   status ∈ {queued, in_progress} AND owning workflow_run is in
   a terminal state → force-complete as neutral + log `zombie-swept`
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — leak-free creation:** for every placeholder P registered by a cycle, the cycle's termination (any path, including process kill between register and dispatch) results in P being terminal within one SM tick. There is no code path that leaves P open.
- **I2 — detection is grounded, not heuristic:** the sweeper never force-completes a check-run whose owning workflow run is still live. A live `in_progress` `Quality gate` is legitimate; only terminal-owner + open-check is a zombie.
- **I3 — required-check semantics preserved:** placeholder conclusions always mirror the cycle's real outcome (never a blanket `success`), so GitHub's required-check verdict stays truthful. `neutral` is reserved for superseded cycles — a superseded cycle carries no verdict about its head.
- **I4 — creator-only boundary respected:** all close operations run under the same app identity that created the check-runs (the cycle's own token); no cross-app completion is attempted, because GitHub rejects it (404) by design.
- **I5 — observability:** every close and every sweep action leaves a machine-log line (`check-close: <run-id> <conclusion>` / `zombie-swept: <check-run-id> head <sha>`); zombies found by the sweeper are counted in the factory state payload so operators see the leak rate, not just the fix.

## Capability surface (every cycle outcome → close obligation)

| Cycle outcome | Placeholders closed today? | Must close (this card) | Conclusion value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation success | NO (live instance: success run, open placeholder) | YES — core | `success` |
| Validation failure | unknown, assumed NO (same path) | YES — core | `failure` (keeps the PR honestly parked) |
| Superseded by newer head H' | NO | YES — core | `neutral` (no verdict carried across heads) |
| Cycle cancelled (dup dispatch, timeout) | NO | YES — core | `neutral` |
| Process died between register and dispatch | NO | YES — core (recovered by finally-on-next-tick) | `neutral` |
| Pre-fix leaked zombies on existing PRs | n/a | YES — sweeper, second tier | `neutral` + count metric |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I5 for all rows above; the finally-path lives in the SAME job that registers placeholders, so it inherits the creator token (I4 for free).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** the sweeper generalizes to a periodic (hourly) repo-wide scan for terminal-owner open checks on ANY ref, plus a factory-state metric page for the leak counter.
- **Excluded (rationale):** completing OTHER apps' check-runs (GitHub forbids; listed as *impossible*, not excluded-by-taste); changing the required-check configuration (repo settings are out of scope); converting placeholders to real job-based checks (a larger redesign — follow-up card if desired).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: the placeholder-lifecycle state machine transitions register→(success|failure|superseded|cancelled|died)→closed with the correct conclusion per the table; no transition leaves the object open. *Hook: pure state-machine UT over the five outcomes.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub API): a scripted cycle that registers 3 placeholders, then terminates with each of the five outcomes → each placeholder receives exactly one close call with the mapped conclusion; a kill between register and dispatch is recovered by the next tick's finally. *Hook: scripted API fixture with call assertions.*
- **AC3** — Zombie detection: given a check-run with `status=in_progress` whose `check_suite`/`workflow_run` is terminal, the sweeper force-completes it as `neutral` and emits the `zombie-swept` log line; a live-owner `in_progress` check is never touched. *Hook: IT with two fixtures (terminal owner vs live owner).*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox repo): reproduce the fa #1563 shape — kicker push → placeholders → superseding push → real CI green on the final head → PR mergeable WITHOUT any human or sweeper intervention, because no zombie exists on the final head. *Hook: E2E scenario named `zombie-repro-1563`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded fa #1563 timeline (suite 105847141092, check-run 117469671401) against the sweeper → the check-run ends terminal as `neutral`, the metric increments, and the PR's computed mergeability flips to the real (green) verdict. *Hook: REG fixture from the live incident; CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green…

blocks.text:
Key observations so far:

1. **The sweep target set** (`vOrphans` via `orphanedRunChecks`) is NOT filtered to the github-actions App's own check-runs — it includes ANY pending check-run with a terminal owning run. For a third-party app's check-run (e.g., codecov), the PATCH will fail with 403/404 → `out.rejected` set, warns every tick, retries forever. This is the same exposure gh-865's conclude has (pre-existing), but the new sweep runs in a strictly broader trigger condition (previously the whole block required green probe; now any non-green head with orphans triggers PATCH attempts). However: gh-865's in-place conclude already had this exposure in the green case. The neutral sweep broadens it to every red/no-verdict head. Still, real-world check-runs with linked workflow runs are usually GitHub Actions ones; third-party check runs typically don't have a workflow_run link, so runIdOf would be null and they'd be excluded. So the risk is moderate-low. Could flag as SUGESTION (filter to own-app or mark-and-skip persistent rejections).

2. **Behavioral gating concern — the gh-857 gate widening.** Previously: `if (vProbe && vProbe.green && silentToken)`. Now: `if (silentToken)` and inside, phCover is only probed when probe is green. Neutral sweep condition: `vOrphans.length && !(vProbe && vProbe.green)`. So when the probe is RED (validation genuinely failed on this head), the sweep force-completes orphan placeholders as neutral. Per gh-998's capability table, a `failure` outcome should close placeholders as `failure` — closing as `neutral` when the cycle actually failed... Hmm, wait: if the probe is red, the head HAS a real failure verdict (from the dispatched run). The placeholder zombie is a leak; the required check truth is carried by the red stamp. Neutral for the zombie is fine and arguably the sweper can't do better (it can't re-run the cycle to mint a failure conclusion under the placeholder). Also neutral doesn't unblock a required check gate (neutral typically doesn't satisfy required checks) — the PR stays parked honestly. So no laundering. OK.

3. **A more significant correctness question**: the sweep fires when `vProbe` is missing/null entirely. What is vProbe? Let me check — it's probably the probe of the validation verdict. If vProbe is null because the probe FAILED (couldn't determine), the sweep concludes orphans as neutral even though a green verdict may exist — but wait, if probe failed, gh-857 previously did nothing too (gate required vProbe.green). Closing a zombie as neutral when the head actually has a green verdict in flight... the orphan detector requires the OWNING run to be terminal past grace, so the check-run genuinely is orphaned. Neutral close is honest regardless. And the green cover probe (`greenCoverRun`) is only skipped when probe is not green — but greenCoverRun probes workflow runs directly, independent of vProbe. If vProbe is null (probe error) but a real green cover exists, the sweep closes orphans neutral instead of success-mirroring — mildly suboptimal but not a correctness bug (the genuine green stamp from real CI still exists separately; the neutral placeholder won't override the latest-per-name? Actually branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head) — a neutral conclusion now becomes the latest stamp for that check-run... but it's the same check-run object; the real CI green verdict lives in a DIFFERENT check-run (dispatched run's own check). Per gh-857's fd1b9aa2 lesson, the placeholder being pending blocked despite a later green stamp — "branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head)". Hmm, if contexts differ by name, the placeholder `Quality gate` pending blocked even though a genuine `Quality gate: success` existed. Completing the placeholder neutral removes the pending state; GitHub then evaluates required check `Quality gate` — with one neutral and one success... The live incident says a genuine Quality gate success existed with the zombie pending and the PR was BLOCKED, so pending was the blocker. After neutral close, does the required check resolve to success (latest conclusion?) or neutral? GitHub required check evaluation: for a check run, the latest execution matters? Actually each check-run is per suite; the required status check looks across check-runs by name — GitHub docs: if multiple check runs with the same name, the most recent one (by creation?) is used. The PR description says "a pending required check counts per name across ALL suites on the head". After neutral conclusion, the placeholder is no longer pending — presumably the gate then uses the genuine success. The PR notes acknowledge "the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered". Whether neutral + success = mergeable is GitHub behavior; the PR claims live validation. Can't verify here. Fine.

4. **E2 escalation gap**: ticket E2 says "a persistent failure escalates to an issue (existing alarm path) rather than silently leaking — degradation path". The implementation retries next tick and only console.warns. No escalation. But PR scope notes say E2E/REG and creation-side live elsewhere; the retry-next-tick behavior is described in the PR ("rejections retry next tick (E2)"). The ticket is huge; the PR delivers Q2 sweper + state machine + metric. Escalation could be a follow-up. I'd classify as SUGESTION or IMPORTANT? The machine instruction: IMPORTANT = real maintainability/correctness issue, PR works as shipped. A persistent 403 on every tick → warn every tick forever = log noise, but functionally it just retries. I'd say SUGESTION-to-IMPORTANT. I'll make it a SUGESTION (follow-up card for escalation/marking persistently-rejected check-runs), or IMPORTANT? Given each wasted round costs CI minutes, be conservative — SUGESTION.

5. **`orphanedRunChecks` runs per PR per tick** — `headOrphanedRunChecks` does 2 API calls per head each tick. Pre-existing. The sweep adds one PATCH per orphan. Bounded fine.

6. **`zombiesSwept` cumulative double-count risk**: `buildFactoryState` input.prev = spPrev — the previous published snapshot, and input.zombiesSwept = this tick's count. That's correct cumulative. But note the DRY case: in DRY, `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` increments `out.concluded` in DRY mode, which increments tickZombiesSwept, which rides into... does buildFactoryState/publish run in DRY? publishFactoryState with dryRun: DRY — need to check it doesn't publish in dry. Pre-existing pattern for other counters; likely guarded. Minor.

7. **`hasOwnProperty` direct call**: `CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS.hasOwnProperty(outcome)` — safe on a plain object literal. If outcome is null/undefined → returns false → null. Fine. Style: repo may prefer Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call, but the object is a sealed literal — fine.

8. **Test for the sweper transport missing**: `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` in smAgent.js has NO direct unit test (smAgent transports historically untestable in unit runner? gh-857 conclude also untested directly). Tests cover the pure module only. AC2/AC3 integration hooks (scripted API fixtures) are noted as living in factory/kicker repos. Acceptable per PR notes; could note as SUGESTION. Actually AC3 says "Hook: IT with two fixtures" — detection IT. The detector is gh-865-tested. Sweep behavior (neutral conclusion, log line, retry) is untested at the transport level. Given the repo's unit-test runner can't easily test smAgent transports, this is a known pattern. SUGESTION at most. Hmm — but the review guidelines say "Tests: coverage for new/changed paths". The core riskiest new behavior (the gh-857 gate widening + sweep branch) has zero direct test. The 8 new tests all test the pure state-machine module which... wait, actually — is `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle` actually USED anywhere in production code?! Let me check. The sweper in smAgent does NOT use openCycle/closePlaceholderCycle/conclusionForOutcome — it hardcodes conclusion=neutral! Let me grep.

blocks.text:
Confirmed: `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle`/`conclusionForOutcome`/`CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` are **only used by tests** — dead production code. The actual sweper hardcodes `conclusion=neutral` in the `gh api` PATCH. The capability table's `failure→failure` and `success→success` rows are never exercised by any production caller. This is dead code introduced by the PR — the diff checklist explicitly asks "Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced?" This is a real finding: the AC1 state machine was delivered as a pure module with no production consumer. The PR description frames it as "the SM-side finally-path" but the finally-path per-outcome mapping isn't wired — the sweper always uses neutral. That's an IMPORTANT finding (dead code + the capability table not actually driving any close; also misleading: failure-row placeholders get neutral, not failure, when the cycle failed... wait — no: if the cycle failed, is the orphan's owner terminal with conclusion=failure? The sweper could have read the owning run's conclusion and mapped it via conclusionForOutcome! The owner run's conclusion IS available in the orphan detector output path (resolveRun returns state.conclusion). The detector discards the conclusion though (`out.push({name, runId, id, reason})` — no conclusion). So a failure cycle's zombie gets neutral instead of failure. I3 honesty: neutral is not a blanket success so no merge-laundering, but the capability table claims failure→failure and the implementation can't deliver it. However, closing as `failure` would arguably be worse: a failure conclusion on the placeholder check-run name could make the required check red even if a re-dispatch later goes green... Actually per the incident, latest check-run per name wins; a red placeholder might pin the gate red. Neutral is the safer engineering choice. But then the capability table + state machine is aspirational dead code.

Per the verdict rules: is this BLOCKING? It's not a bug that breaks behavior — the shipped sweper works. It's dead code / scope artifact. "Scope violations" count as BLOCKING per the machine rules... The dead state machine IS part of the ticket's AC1 (unit-level state machine), so it's in scope of the ticket, just not wired. The ticket AC1 hook is literally "pure state-machine UT over the five outcomes" — so AC1's deliverable is the pure module + UT. The wiring into the finally-path is the kicker/factory side (out of repo). So arguably not scope violation: the ticket divides core vs. second tier, and Q1 notes the creation-side finally lives in the kicker. But this PR claims "the SM-side finally-path + sweper". The state machine here will presumably be consumed by the kicker-side helper later (shared helper Q1). So dead-until-cross-repo-integration. I'd classify IMPORTANT (dead code in production module, should either be wired or noted as staged-for-kicker with a tracking reference), not BLOCKING. Since no BLOCKING → APPROVE.

Other findings:

A. **Sweep branch can fire on genuinely-red heads every tick for non-Actions check-runs** — rejected loop noise. SUGESTION.

B. **Token restore edge**: if `appToken` set but `sourceTok` undefined, GH_TOKEN stays as appToken after sweep (same pattern in gh-857 pre-existing). Not new — skip or mention? The new function copies the existing pattern including the flaw. Since the whole block is gated on silentToken presence and sourceToken presumably always accompanies it, minor. Could mention as SUGESTION (restore to unset rather than leave swapped when sourceTok missing). Actually compare: same flaw exists in concludePlaceholderCheckRuns (pre-existing). Flag once as SUGESTION on the new function.

C. **DRY-mode counter pollution**: in DRY, `out.concluded++` increments tickZombiesSwept which rides into state payload — but publish in DRY... `publishFactoryState(spState, spCfg, ...)` — is publish skipped in DRY? Let me check quickly. If it publishes even in dry, the metric lies in dry runs (dry runs presumably don't publish — check).

D. **The gh-857 gate widening removed `vProbe && vProbe.green` from the outer condition** — meaning `phHeadRuns` API calls now happen on every head with placeholders/orphans even when probe is red. That's +2 gh api calls per PR per tick in the red case. Perf, negligible.

E. **`zombiesSweptTotal` handles prev correctly; call site passes spPrev** — verified spPrev at line 410. Good. But does `spPrev` include `zombiesSwept` from the published snapshot? spPrev = previous published snapshot parsed → yes it will contain the field from last tick. Good.

F. Check CI: input has no ci_failures.md. The discussions mention an earlier CRAP failure that was fixed (buildFactoryState back to 65.1, ratchet exit 0). The latest head 874691b7... wait, git log shows the local branch has a6b6093d "pr-1012 WIP auto-save" and 07f6cea7 merge of origin/main on top. The PR info says updated 2026-10-18T09:26. Discussions mention full suite 3867 passed. No CI failure file present → treat as no known red CI. But wait — the ticket "Machine jobs" shows the rework job 🚫 (fa-rework run 3912942777 "done 08:51 🚫"). That's the rework run that failed? It says dev (fa-rework) done 🚫. Hmm, that might be the CRAP failure lap. The subsequent discussion shows the CRAP fix with ratchet exit 0 and full suite green on head 874691b. And a later lap pushed at 09:26 resolving 2 threads. Since no ci_failures.md provided, and per rules "If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as BLOCKING" — it's absent. I'll note the earlier CRAP regression appears resolved per the discussion (rework summary shows ratchet exit 0, baseline-exact).

Should I run the tests locally? The PR description says full suite passes. Running the focused new test suites would be good verification. Let me run node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js on the two test files.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:

callers/callees of changed symbols,

impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. - **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:26:39Z

## PR Description

Closes #998
### Root Cause
A placeholder check-run in `in_progress` whose owning workflow run terminated had no close path for four of the five cycle outcomes: the gh-857 in-place conclusion only mirrors a **green** verdict (and only with a probed green cover, no active head run, and an app token). Failure/superseded/cancelled/died cycles and all pre-fix leaks left the zombie pinned to its SHA — mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED forever (live fa #1563, head `f3d58647`, check-run 117469671401), and the legacy same-sha re-dispatch cannot conclude a stamp nothing will conclude.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — gh-998 lifecycle contract: `CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` + `conclusionForOutcome` (capability table), `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle` (AC1 state machine over the five outcomes; unknown outcome fails safe, double-close rejected — E1 idempotence), `zombieSweptLine` (I5 log format).
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-998 neutral sweep in the validate-pr placeholder/orphan block: terminal-owner orphans (gh-865 detector) whose cycle left no verdict are force-completed as `neutral` under the cycle's own app token (I3/I4), with the gh-857 AC2 fail-safes unchanged (no active head run; green-probe corner falls through untouched). New transport `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` emits `zombie-swept: <id> head <sha>` per close; rejections retry next tick (E2). Per-tick counter reset in `action()`.
- `js/factoryState.js` — cumulative `zombiesSwept` rides the state snapshot (I5); smAgent passes the tick count at the `buildFactoryState` call site.
- Link-less placeholders deliberately keep the gh-852 fresh-sha reset (a same-sha re-dispatch re-mints them — only a fresh head cures that pathology, gh-852 AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — 8 new tests: conclusion mapping, five-outcome lifecycle (incl. 3-placeholder multi-item), fail-safe unknown outcome, idempotent double-close rejection, `zombie-swept` log line. RED first (8 failed), GREEN after implementation.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 4 new tests: stable-shape 0, tick count, cumulative carry, malformed-carry restart.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **3590 passed, 0 failed** (clean-env re-run: 3538 passed, 0 failed — delta is env-dependent skips; new suites pass 49/49 and 145/145 standalone).

### Notes
- The creation-side finally-path for the kicker stub (Q1, shared helper) and the E2E/REG sandbox scenarios (AC4/AC5) live in the factory/kicker repos and CI — out of this repo's reach; this change is the SM-side finally-path + sweper (Q2 per-tick piggyback) + observability.
- A `neutral` close is honest but not a green verdict: the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered (I3).
