# gh-998: Zombie in_progress check-run survives head change and blocks merge forever (fa #1563 live)

## Description

## Goal — leaked placeholder check-runs become unreachable, and existing zombies get swept (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **a check-run in state `in_progress`/`queued` whose owning workflow run has already terminated becomes unreachable state** — every cycle that opens placeholder check-runs closes them in a finally-path, every superseded cycle force-completes its leftovers, and a sweeper heals check-runs leaked before this fix.

Today the kicker registers long-lived placeholder check-runs (e.g. `Quality gate`, `JS engine integration`, `Binaries smoke gate`) on a fresh head so the PR shows "under validation" while the real gate is a dispatch-only workflow; when the cycle is superseded (new head, re-dispatch, cancellation) or ends, the placeholders are not closed. A leaked `in_progress` check is pinned to its SHA forever: GitHub computes the required-check state per name across ALL suites on the head, so ONE zombie `Quality gate` holds `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even when 58 sibling checks are green and a genuine `Quality gate: success` exists from the real CI run. The merge bot then waits `checks=pending` every tick and the PR cannot merge by any machine action — the branch is not behind, so no re-validation cycle helps.

Live instance 2026-10-17 (fa #1563, head `f3d58647`): suite 105847141092 created by the kicker push at 18:15:41Z; placeholder `Quality gate` registered 18:24:18Z (check-run id 117469671401) stayed `in_progress` 40+ minutes past its cycle; PR hard-stuck at BLOCKED; operator could not close it via REST (`POST /check-runs/{id}/completed` → 404: only the creating app may complete its own check-runs). The PR only escaped because it merged by other means. Closing that escape hatch is what makes this card load-bearing.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "close zombie check-runs by hand via API when found." Impossible in practice (creator-only restriction) and wrong in principle (see owner directive on dmtools-agents#994: manual cleanup masks the bug; the pipeline must not depend on humans GC-ing its leaks).
- **Retracted:** "the merge bot should treat in_progress checks whose workflow run completed as stale." That is the *detection* half and survives only as an input to the sweeper; the *cure* must be closing the leak at creation time plus healing what already leaked.
- **Retracted:** "wait for the next head — zombies die with their SHA." True only while the head keeps moving; a green, up-to-date, fully-validated PR with a zombie on its CURRENT head (the live instance) has no reason to move. A system where the only cure is generating new work is a leak with extra steps.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle (subject of every verb is the **check-run object**, owned by a **validation cycle** keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
cycle start (kicker/rework/operator push → new head H)
   │ registers placeholders P1..Pn on H via Checks API
   ▼
validation dispatched (dispatch-only CI, separate workflow)
   │ outcomes: success | failure | superseded (new head H') | cancelled
   ▼
finally-path [THE FIX — runs for EVERY outcome]
   ├── close P1..Pn on H with the cycle's real conclusion
   │      (success→success, failure→failure, superseded→neutral)
   └── force-complete any P_i still queued/in_progress even if the
       closing call itself failed (retry w/ backoff, then escalate)
        │
        ▼
[sweeper — self-heal pre-fix leaks]
   scan heads of open, non-dirty PRs for check-runs where
   status ∈ {queued, in_progress} AND owning workflow_run is in
   a terminal state → force-complete as neutral + log `zombie-swept`
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — leak-free creation:** for every placeholder P registered by a cycle, the cycle's termination (any path, including process kill between register and dispatch) results in P being terminal within one SM tick. There is no code path that leaves P open.
- **I2 — detection is grounded, not heuristic:** the sweeper never force-completes a check-run whose owning workflow run is still live. A live `in_progress` `Quality gate` is legitimate; only terminal-owner + open-check is a zombie.
- **I3 — required-check semantics preserved:** placeholder conclusions always mirror the cycle's real outcome (never a blanket `success`), so GitHub's required-check verdict stays truthful. `neutral` is reserved for superseded cycles — a superseded cycle carries no verdict about its head.
- **I4 — creator-only boundary respected:** all close operations run under the same app identity that created the check-runs (the cycle's own token); no cross-app completion is attempted, because GitHub rejects it (404) by design.
- **I5 — observability:** every close and every sweep action leaves a machine-log line (`check-close: <run-id> <conclusion>` / `zombie-swept: <check-run-id> head <sha>`); zombies found by the sweeper are counted in the factory state payload so operators see the leak rate, not just the fix.

## Capability surface (every cycle outcome → close obligation)

| Cycle outcome | Placeholders closed today? | Must close (this card) | Conclusion value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation success | NO (live instance: success run, open placeholder) | YES — core | `success` |
| Validation failure | unknown, assumed NO (same path) | YES — core | `failure` (keeps the PR honestly parked) |
| Superseded by newer head H' | NO | YES — core | `neutral` (no verdict carried across heads) |
| Cycle cancelled (dup dispatch, timeout) | NO | YES — core | `neutral` |
| Process died between register and dispatch | NO | YES — core (recovered by finally-on-next-tick) | `neutral` |
| Pre-fix leaked zombies on existing PRs | n/a | YES — sweeper, second tier | `neutral` + count metric |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I5 for all rows above; the finally-path lives in the SAME job that registers placeholders, so it inherits the creator token (I4 for free).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** the sweeper generalizes to a periodic (hourly) repo-wide scan for terminal-owner open checks on ANY ref, plus a factory-state metric page for the leak counter.
- **Excluded (rationale):** completing OTHER apps' check-runs (GitHub forbids; listed as *impossible*, not excluded-by-taste); changing the required-check configuration (repo settings are out of scope); converting placeholders to real job-based checks (a larger redesign — follow-up card if desired).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: the placeholder-lifecycle state machine transitions register→(success|failure|superseded|cancelled|died)→closed with the correct conclusion per the table; no transition leaves the object open. *Hook: pure state-machine UT over the five outcomes.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub API): a scripted cycle that registers 3 placeholders, then terminates with each of the five outcomes → each placeholder receives exactly one close call with the mapped conclusion; a kill between register and dispatch is recovered by the next tick's finally. *Hook: scripted API fixture with call assertions.*
- **AC3** — Zombie detection: given a check-run with `status=in_progress` whose `check_suite`/`workflow_run` is terminal, the sweeper force-completes it as `neutral` and emits the `zombie-swept` log line; a live-owner `in_progress` check is never touched. *Hook: IT with two fixtures (terminal owner vs live owner).*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox repo): reproduce the fa #1563 shape — kicker push → placeholders → superseding push → real CI green on the final head → PR mergeable WITHOUT any human or sweeper intervention, because no zombie exists on the final head. *Hook: E2E scenario named `zombie-repro-1563`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded fa #1563 timeline (suite 105847141092, check-run 117469671401) against the sweeper → the check-run ends terminal as `neutral`, the metric increments, and the PR's computed mergeability flips to the real (green) verdict. *Hook: REG fixture from the live incident; CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green…

Key observations so far:

1. **The sweep target set** (`vOrphans` via `orphanedRunChecks`) is NOT filtered to the github-actions App's own check-runs — it includes ANY pending check-run with a terminal owning run. For a third-party app's check-run (e.g., codecov), the PATCH will fail with 403/404 → `out.rejected` set, warns every tick, retries forever. This is the same exposure gh-865's conclude has (pre-existing), but the new sweep runs in a strictly broader trigger condition (previously the whole block required green probe; now any non-green head with orphans triggers PATCH attempts). However: gh-865's in-place conclude already had this exposure in the green case. The neutral sweep broadens it to every red/no-verdict head. Still, real-world check-runs with linked workflow runs are usually GitHub Actions ones; third-party check runs typically don't have a workflow_run link, so runIdOf would be null and they'd be excluded. So the risk is moderate-low. Could flag as SUGESTION (filter to own-app or mark-and-skip persistent rejections).

2. **Behavioral gating concern — the gh-857 gate widening.** Previously: `if (vProbe && vProbe.green && silentToken)`. Now: `if (silentToken)` and inside, phCover is only probed when probe is green. Neutral sweep condition: `vOrphans.length && !(vProbe && vProbe.green)`. So when the probe is RED (validation genuinely failed on this head), the sweep force-completes orphan placeholders as neutral. Per gh-998's capability table, a `failure` outcome should close placeholders as `failure` — closing as `neutral` when the cycle actually failed... - **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:26:39Z

## PR Description

Closes #998
### Root Cause
A placeholder check-run in `in_progress` whose owning workflow run terminated had no close path for four of the five cycle outcomes: the gh-857 in-place conclusion only mirrors a **green** verdict (and only with a probed green cover, no active head run, and an app token). Failure/superseded/cancelled/died cycles and all pre-fix leaks left the zombie pinned to its SHA — mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED forever (live fa #1563, head `f3d58647`, check-run 117469671401), and the legacy same-sha re-dispatch cannot conclude a stamp nothing will conclude.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — gh-998 lifecycle contract: `CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` + `conclusionForOutcome` (capability table), `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle` (AC1 state machine over the five outcomes; unknown outcome fails safe, double-close rejected — E1 idempotence), `zombieSweptLine` (I5 log format).
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-998 neutral sweep in the validate-pr placeholder/orphan block: terminal-owner orphans (gh-865 detector) whose cycle left no verdict are force-completed as `neutral` under the cycle's own app token (I3/I4), with the gh-857 AC2 fail-safes unchanged (no active head run; green-probe corner falls through untouched). New transport `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` emits `zombie-swept: <id> head <sha>` per close; rejections retry next tick (E2). Per-tick counter reset in `action()`.
- `js/factoryState.js` — cumulative `zombiesSwept` rides the state snapshot (I5); smAgent passes the tick count at the `buildFactoryState` call site.
- Link-less placeholders deliberately keep the gh-852 fresh-sha reset (a same-sha re-dispatch re-mints them — only a fresh head cures that pathology, gh-852 AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — 8 new tests: conclusion mapping, five-outcome lifecycle (incl. 3-placeholder multi-item), fail-safe unknown outcome, idempotent double-close rejection, `zombie-swept` log line. RED first (8 failed), GREEN after implementation.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 4 new tests: stable-shape 0, tick count, cumulative carry, malformed-carry restart.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **3590 passed, 0 failed** (clean-env re-run: 3538 passed, 0 failed — delta is env-dependent skips; new suites pass 49/49 and 145/145 standalone).

### Notes
- The creation-side finally-path for the kicker stub (Q1, shared helper) and the E2E/REG sandbox scenarios (AC4/AC5) live in the factory/kicker repos and CI — out of this repo's reach; this change is the SM-side finally-path + sweper (Q2 per-tick piggyback) + observability.
- A `neutral` close is honest but not a green verdict: the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered (I3).

# gh-998: Zombie in_progress check-run survives head change and blocks merge forever (fa #1563 live)

## Description

## Goal — leaked placeholder check-runs become unreachable, and existing zombies get swept (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **a check-run in state `in_progress`/`queued` whose owning workflow run has already terminated becomes unreachable state** — every cycle that opens placeholder check-runs closes them in a finally-path, every superseded cycle force-completes its leftovers, and a sweeper heals check-runs leaked before this fix.

Today the kicker registers long-lived placeholder check-runs (e.g. `Quality gate`, `JS engine integration`, `Binaries smoke gate`) on a fresh head so the PR shows "under validation" while the real gate is a dispatch-only workflow; when the cycle is superseded (new head, re-dispatch, cancellation) or ends, the placeholders are not closed. A leaked `in_progress` check is pinned to its SHA forever: GitHub computes the required-check state per name across ALL suites on the head, so ONE zombie `Quality gate` holds `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even when 58 sibling checks are green and a genuine `Quality gate: success` exists from the real CI run. The merge bot then waits `checks=pending` every tick and the PR cannot merge by any machine action — the branch is not behind, so no re-validation cycle helps.

Live instance 2026-10-17 (fa #1563, head `f3d58647`): suite 105847141092 created by the kicker push at 18:15:41Z; placeholder `Quality gate` registered 18:24:18Z (check-run id 117469671401) stayed `in_progress` 40+ minutes past its cycle; PR hard-stuck at BLOCKED; operator could not close it via REST (`POST /check-runs/{id}/completed` → 404: only the creating app may complete its own check-runs). The PR only escaped because it merged by other means. Closing that escape hatch is what makes this card load-bearing.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "close zombie check-runs by hand via API when found." Impossible in practice (creator-only restriction) and wrong in principle (see owner directive on dmtools-agents#994: manual cleanup masks the bug; the pipeline must not depend on humans GC-ing its leaks).
- **Retracted:** "the merge bot should treat in_progress checks whose workflow run completed as stale." That is the *detection* half and survives only as an input to the sweeper; the *cure* must be closing the leak at creation time plus healing what already leaked.
- **Retracted:** "wait for the next head — zombies die with their SHA." True only while the head keeps moving; a green, up-to-date, fully-validated PR with a zombie on its CURRENT head (the live instance) has no reason to move. A system where the only cure is generating new work is a leak with extra steps.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle (subject of every verb is the **check-run object**, owned by a **validation cycle** keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
cycle start (kicker/rework/operator push → new head H)
   │ registers placeholders P1..Pn on H via Checks API
   ▼
validation dispatched (dispatch-only CI, separate workflow)
   │ outcomes: success | failure | superseded (new head H') | cancelled
   ▼
finally-path [THE FIX — runs for EVERY outcome]
   ├── close P1..Pn on H with the cycle's real conclusion
   │      (success→success, failure→failure, superseded→neutral)
   └── force-complete any P_i still queued/in_progress even if the
       closing call itself failed (retry w/ backoff, then escalate)
        │
        ▼
[sweeper — self-heal pre-fix leaks]
   scan heads of open, non-dirty PRs for check-runs where
   status ∈ {queued, in_progress} AND owning workflow_run is in
   a terminal state → force-complete as neutral + log `zombie-swept`
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — leak-free creation:** for every placeholder P registered by a cycle, the cycle's termination (any path, including process kill between register and dispatch) results in P being terminal within one SM tick. There is no code path that leaves P open.
- **I2 — detection is grounded, not heuristic:** the sweeper never force-completes a check-run whose owning workflow run is still live. A live `in_progress` `Quality gate` is legitimate; only terminal-owner + open-check is a zombie.
- **I3 — required-check semantics preserved:** placeholder conclusions always mirror the cycle's real outcome (never a blanket `success`), so GitHub's required-check verdict stays truthful. `neutral` is reserved for superseded cycles — a superseded cycle carries no verdict about its head.
- **I4 — creator-only boundary respected:** all close operations run under the same app identity that created the check-runs (the cycle's own token); no cross-app completion is attempted, because GitHub rejects it (404) by design.
- **I5 — observability:** every close and every sweep action leaves a machine-log line (`check-close: <run-id> <conclusion>` / `zombie-swept: <check-run-id> head <sha>`); zombies found by the sweeper are counted in the factory state payload so operators see the leak rate, not just the fix.

## Capability surface (every cycle outcome → close obligation)

| Cycle outcome | Placeholders closed today? | Must close (this card) | Conclusion value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation success | NO (live instance: success run, open placeholder) | YES — core | `success` |
| Validation failure | unknown, assumed NO (same path) | YES — core | `failure` (keeps the PR honestly parked) |
| Superseded by newer head H' | NO | YES — core | `neutral` (no verdict carried across heads) |
| Cycle cancelled (dup dispatch, timeout) | NO | YES — core | `neutral` |
| Process died between register and dispatch | NO | YES — core (recovered by finally-on-next-tick) | `neutral` |
| Pre-fix leaked zombies on existing PRs | n/a | YES — sweeper, second tier | `neutral` + count metric |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I5 for all rows above; the finally-path lives in the SAME job that registers placeholders, so it inherits the creator token (I4 for free).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** the sweeper generalizes to a periodic (hourly) repo-wide scan for terminal-owner open checks on ANY ref, plus a factory-state metric page for the leak counter.
- **Excluded (rationale):** completing OTHER apps' check-runs (GitHub forbids; listed as *impossible*, not excluded-by-taste); changing the required-check configuration (repo settings are out of scope); converting placeholders to real job-based checks (a larger redesign — follow-up card if desired).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: the placeholder-lifecycle state machine transitions register→(success|failure|superseded|cancelled|died)→closed with the correct conclusion per the table; no transition leaves the object open. *Hook: pure state-machine UT over the five outcomes.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub API): a scripted cycle that registers 3 placeholders, then terminates with each of the five outcomes → each placeholder receives exactly one close call with the mapped conclusion; a kill between register and dispatch is recovered by the next tick's finally. *Hook: scripted API fixture with call assertions.*
- **AC3** — Zombie detection: given a check-run with `status=in_progress` whose `check_suite`/`workflow_run` is terminal, the sweeper force-completes it as `neutral` and emits the `zombie-swept` log line; a live-owner `in_progress` check is never touched. *Hook: IT with two fixtures (terminal owner vs live owner).*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox repo): reproduce the fa #1563 shape — kicker push → placeholders → superseding push → real CI green on the final head → PR mergeable WITHOUT any human or sweeper intervention, because no zombie exists on the final head. *Hook: E2E scenario named `zombie-repro-1563`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded fa #1563 timeline (suite 105847141092, check-run 117469671401) against the sweeper → the check-run ends terminal as `neutral`, the metric increments, and the PR's computed mergeability flips to the real (green) verdict. *Hook: REG fixture from the live incident; CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green…

Key observations so far:

1. **The sweep target set** (`vOrphans` via `orphanedRunChecks`) is NOT filtered to the github-actions App's own check-runs — it includes ANY pending check-run with a terminal owning run. For a third-party app's check-run (e.g., codecov), the PATCH will fail with 403/404 → `out.rejected` set, warns every tick, retries forever. This is the same exposure gh-865's conclude has (pre-existing), but the new sweep runs in a strictly broader trigger condition (previously the whole block required green probe; now any non-green head with orphans triggers PATCH attempts). However: gh-865's in-place conclude already had this exposure in the green case. The neutral sweep broadens it to every red/no-verdict head. Still, real-world check-runs with linked workflow runs are usually GitHub Actions ones; third-party check runs typically don't have a workflow_run link, so runIdOf would be null and they'd be excluded. So the risk is moderate-low. Could flag as SUGESTION (filter to own-app or mark-and-skip persistent rejections).

2. **Behavioral gating concern — the gh-857 gate widening.** Previously: `if (vProbe && vProbe.green && silentToken)`. Now: `if (silentToken)` and inside, phCover is only probed when probe is green. Neutral sweep condition: `vOrphans.length && !(vProbe && vProbe.green)`. So when the probe is RED (validation genuinely failed on this head), the sweep force-completes orphan placeholders as neutral. Per gh-998's capability table, a `failure` outcome should close placeholders as `failure` — closing as `neutral` when the cycle actually failed... Hmm, wait: if the probe is red, the head HAS a real failure verdict (from the dispatched run). The placeholder zombie is a leak; the required check truth is carried by the red stamp. Neutral for the zombie is fine and arguably the sweper can't do better (it can't re-run the cycle to mint a failure conclusion under the placeholder). Also neutral doesn't unblock a required check gate (neutral typically doesn't satisfy required checks) — the PR stays parked honestly. So no laundering. OK.

3. **A more significant correctness question**: the sweep fires when `vProbe` is missing/null entirely. What is vProbe? Let me check — it's probably the probe of the validation verdict. If vProbe is null because the probe FAILED (couldn't determine), the sweep concludes orphans as neutral even though a green verdict may exist — but wait, if probe failed, gh-857 previously did nothing too (gate required vProbe.green). Closing a zombie as neutral when the head actually has a green verdict in flight... the orphan detector requires the OWNING run to be terminal past grace, so the check-run genuinely is orphaned. Neutral close is honest regardless. And the green cover probe (`greenCoverRun`) is only skipped when probe is not green — but greenCoverRun probes workflow runs directly, independent of vProbe. - **Deletions**: -2

- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:26:39Z

## PR Description

Closes #998
### Root Cause
A placeholder check-run in `in_progress` whose owning workflow run terminated had no close path for four of the five cycle outcomes: the gh-857 in-place conclusion only mirrors a **green** verdict (and only with a probed green cover, no active head run, and an app token). Failure/superseded/cancelled/died cycles and all pre-fix leaks left the zombie pinned to its SHA — mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED forever (live fa #1563, head `f3d58647`, check-run 117469671401), and the legacy same-sha re-dispatch cannot conclude a stamp nothing will conclude.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — gh-998 lifecycle contract: `CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` + `conclusionForOutcome` (capability table), `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle` (AC1 state machine over the five outcomes; unknown outcome fails safe, double-close rejected — E1 idempotence), `zombieSweptLine` (I5 log format).
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-998 neutral sweep in the validate-pr placeholder/orphan block: terminal-owner orphans (gh-865 detector) whose cycle left no verdict are force-completed as `neutral` under the cycle's own app token (I3/I4), with the gh-857 AC2 fail-safes unchanged (no active head run; green-probe corner falls through untouched). New transport `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` emits `zombie-swept: <id> head <sha>` per close; rejections retry next tick (E2). Per-tick counter reset in `action()`.
- `js/factoryState.js` — cumulative `zombiesSwept` rides the state snapshot (I5); smAgent passes the tick count at the `buildFactoryState` call site.
- Link-less placeholders deliberately keep the gh-852 fresh-sha reset (a same-sha re-dispatch re-mints them — only a fresh head cures that pathology, gh-852 AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — 8 new tests: conclusion mapping, five-outcome lifecycle (incl. 3-placeholder multi-item), fail-safe unknown outcome, idempotent double-close rejection, `zombie-swept` log line. RED first (8 failed), GREEN after implementation.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 4 new tests: stable-shape 0, tick count, cumulative carry, malformed-carry restart.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **3590 passed, 0 failed** (clean-env re-run: 3538 passed, 0 failed — delta is env-dependent skips; new suites pass 49/49 and 145/145 standalone).

### Notes
- The creation-side finally-path for the kicker stub (Q1, shared helper) and the E2E/REG sandbox scenarios (AC4/AC5) live in the factory/kicker repos and CI — out of this repo's reach; this change is the SM-side finally-path + sweper (Q2 per-tick piggyback) + observability.
- A `neutral` close is honest but not a green verdict: the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered (I3).

# gh-998: Zombie in_progress check-run survives head change and blocks merge forever (fa #1563 live)

## Description

## Goal — leaked placeholder check-runs become unreachable, and existing zombies get swept (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **a check-run in state `in_progress`/`queued` whose owning workflow run has already terminated becomes unreachable state** — every cycle that opens placeholder check-runs closes them in a finally-path, every superseded cycle force-completes its leftovers, and a sweeper heals check-runs leaked before this fix.

Today the kicker registers long-lived placeholder check-runs (e.g. `Quality gate`, `JS engine integration`, `Binaries smoke gate`) on a fresh head so the PR shows "under validation" while the real gate is a dispatch-only workflow; when the cycle is superseded (new head, re-dispatch, cancellation) or ends, the placeholders are not closed. A leaked `in_progress` check is pinned to its SHA forever: GitHub computes the required-check state per name across ALL suites on the head, so ONE zombie `Quality gate` holds `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even when 58 sibling checks are green and a genuine `Quality gate: success` exists from the real CI run. The merge bot then waits `checks=pending` every tick and the PR cannot merge by any machine action — the branch is not behind, so no re-validation cycle helps.

Live instance 2026-10-17 (fa #1563, head `f3d58647`): suite 105847141092 created by the kicker push at 18:15:41Z; placeholder `Quality gate` registered 18:24:18Z (check-run id 117469671401) stayed `in_progress` 40+ minutes past its cycle; PR hard-stuck at BLOCKED; operator could not close it via REST (`POST /check-runs/{id}/completed` → 404: only the creating app may complete its own check-runs). The PR only escaped because it merged by other means. Closing that escape hatch is what makes this card load-bearing.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "close zombie check-runs by hand via API when found." Impossible in practice (creator-only restriction) and wrong in principle (see owner directive on dmtools-agents#994: manual cleanup masks the bug; the pipeline must not depend on humans GC-ing its leaks).
- **Retracted:** "the merge bot should treat in_progress checks whose workflow run completed as stale." That is the *detection* half and survives only as an input to the sweeper; the *cure* must be closing the leak at creation time plus healing what already leaked.
- **Retracted:** "wait for the next head — zombies die with their SHA." True only while the head keeps moving; a green, up-to-date, fully-validated PR with a zombie on its CURRENT head (the live instance) has no reason to move. A system where the only cure is generating new work is a leak with extra steps.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle (subject of every verb is the **check-run object**, owned by a **validation cycle** keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
cycle start (kicker/rework/operator push → new head H)
   │ registers placeholders P1..Pn on H via Checks API
   ▼
validation dispatched (dispatch-only CI, separate workflow)
   │ outcomes: success | failure | superseded (new head H') | cancelled
   ▼
finally-path [THE FIX — runs for EVERY outcome]
   ├── close P1..Pn on H with the cycle's real conclusion
   │      (success→success, failure→failure, superseded→neutral)
   └── force-complete any P_i still queued/in_progress even if the
       closing call itself failed (retry w/ backoff, then escalate)
        │
        ▼
[sweeper — self-heal pre-fix leaks]
   scan heads of open, non-dirty PRs for check-runs where
   status ∈ {queued, in_progress} AND owning workflow_run is in
   a terminal state → force-complete as neutral + log `zombie-swept`
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — leak-free creation:** for every placeholder P registered by a cycle, the cycle's termination (any path, including process kill between register and dispatch) results in P being terminal within one SM tick. There is no code path that leaves P open.
- **I2 — detection is grounded, not heuristic:** the sweeper never force-completes a check-run whose owning workflow run is still live. A live `in_progress` `Quality gate` is legitimate; only terminal-owner + open-check is a zombie.
- **I3 — required-check semantics preserved:** placeholder conclusions always mirror the cycle's real outcome (never a blanket `success`), so GitHub's required-check verdict stays truthful. `neutral` is reserved for superseded cycles — a superseded cycle carries no verdict about its head.
- **I4 — creator-only boundary respected:** all close operations run under the same app identity that created the check-runs (the cycle's own token); no cross-app completion is attempted, because GitHub rejects it (404) by design.
- **I5 — observability:** every close and every sweep action leaves a machine-log line (`check-close: <run-id> <conclusion>` / `zombie-swept: <check-run-id> head <sha>`); zombies found by the sweeper are counted in the factory state payload so operators see the leak rate, not just the fix.

## Capability surface (every cycle outcome → close obligation)

| Cycle outcome | Placeholders closed today? | Must close (this card) | Conclusion value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation success | NO (live instance: success run, open placeholder) | YES — core | `success` |
| Validation failure | unknown, assumed NO (same path) | YES — core | `failure` (keeps the PR honestly parked) |
| Superseded by newer head H' | NO | YES — core | `neutral` (no verdict carried across heads) |
| Cycle cancelled (dup dispatch, timeout) | NO | YES — core | `neutral` |
| Process died between register and dispatch | NO | YES — core (recovered by finally-on-next-tick) | `neutral` |
| Pre-fix leaked zombies on existing PRs | n/a | YES — sweeper, second tier | `neutral` + count metric |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I5 for all rows above; the finally-path lives in the SAME job that registers placeholders, so it inherits the creator token (I4 for free).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** the sweeper generalizes to a periodic (hourly) repo-wide scan for terminal-owner open checks on ANY ref, plus a factory-state metric page for the leak counter.
- **Excluded (rationale):** completing OTHER apps' check-runs (GitHub forbids; listed as *impossible*, not excluded-by-taste); changing the required-check configuration (repo settings are out of scope); converting placeholders to real job-based checks (a larger redesign — follow-up card if desired).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: the placeholder-lifecycle state machine transitions register→(success|failure|superseded|cancelled|died)→closed with the correct conclusion per the table; no transition leaves the object open. *Hook: pure state-machine UT over the five outcomes.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub API): a scripted cycle that registers 3 placeholders, then terminates with each of the five outcomes → each placeholder receives exactly one close call with the mapped conclusion; a kill between register and dispatch is recovered by the next tick's finally. *Hook: scripted API fixture with call assertions.*
- **AC3** — Zombie detection: given a check-run with `status=in_progress` whose `check_suite`/`workflow_run` is terminal, the sweeper force-completes it as `neutral` and emits the `zombie-swept` log line; a live-owner `in_progress` check is never touched. *Hook: IT with two fixtures (terminal owner vs live owner).*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox repo): reproduce the fa #1563 shape — kicker push → placeholders → superseding push → real CI green on the final head → PR mergeable WITHOUT any human or sweeper intervention, because no zombie exists on the final head. *Hook: E2E scenario named `zombie-repro-1563`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded fa #1563 timeline (suite 105847141092, check-run 117469671401) against the sweeper → the check-run ends terminal as `neutral`, the metric increments, and the PR's computed mergeability flips to the real (green) verdict. *Hook: REG fixture from the live incident; CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green…

Neutral for the zombie is fine and arguably the sweper can't do better (it can't re-run the cycle to mint a failure conclusion under the placeholder). Also neutral doesn't unblock a required check gate (neutral typically doesn't satisfy required checks) — the PR stays parked honestly. So no laundering. OK.

The live incident says a genuine Quality gate success existed with the zombie pending and the PR was BLOCKED, so pending was the blocker. After neutral conclusion, the placeholder is no longer pending — presumably the gate then uses the genuine success. ## PR Description

Closes #998
### Root Cause
A placeholder check-run in `in_progress` whose owning workflow run terminated had no close path for four of the five cycle outcomes: the gh-857 in-place conclusion only mirrors a **green** verdict (and only with a probed green cover, no active head run, and an app token). Failure/superseded/cancelled/died cycles and all pre-fix leaks left the zombie pinned to its SHA — mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED forever (live fa #1563, head `f3d58647`, check-run 117469671401), and the legacy same-sha re-dispatch cannot conclude a stamp nothing will conclude.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — gh-998 lifecycle contract: `CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` + `conclusionForOutcome` (capability table), `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle` (AC1 state machine over the five outcomes; unknown outcome fails safe, double-close rejected — E1 idempotence), `zombieSweptLine` (I5 log format).
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-998 neutral sweep in the validate-pr placeholder/orphan block: terminal-owner orphans (gh-865 detector) whose cycle left no verdict are force-completed as `neutral` under the cycle's own app token (I3/I4), with the gh-857 AC2 fail-safes unchanged (no active head run; green-probe corner falls through untouched). New transport `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` emits `zombie-swept: <id> head <sha>` per close; rejections retry next tick (E2). Per-tick counter reset in `action()`.
- `js/factoryState.js` — cumulative `zombiesSwept` rides the state snapshot (I5); smAgent passes the tick count at the `buildFactoryState` call site.
- Link-less placeholders deliberately keep the gh-852 fresh-sha reset (a same-sha re-dispatch re-mints them — only a fresh head cures that pathology, gh-852 AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — 8 new tests: conclusion mapping, five-outcome lifecycle (incl. 3-placeholder multi-item), fail-safe unknown outcome, idempotent double-close rejection, `zombie-swept` log line. RED first (8 failed), GREEN after implementation.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 4 new tests: stable-shape 0, tick count, cumulative carry, malformed-carry restart.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **3590 passed, 0 failed** (clean-env re-run: 3538 passed, 0 failed — delta is env-dependent skips; new suites pass 49/49 and 145/145 standalone).

### Notes
- The creation-side finally-path for the kicker stub (Q1, shared helper) and the E2E/REG sandbox scenarios (AC4/AC5) live in the factory/kicker repos and CI — out of this repo's reach; this change is the SM-side finally-path + sweper (Q2 per-tick piggyback) + observability.
- A `neutral` close is honest but not a green verdict: the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered (I3).

# gh-998: Zombie in_progress check-run survives head change and blocks merge forever (fa #1563 live)

## Description

## Goal — leaked placeholder check-runs become unreachable, and existing zombies get swept (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **a check-run in state `in_progress`/`queued` whose owning workflow run has already terminated becomes unreachable state** — every cycle that opens placeholder check-runs closes them in a finally-path, every superseded cycle force-completes its leftovers, and a sweeper heals check-runs leaked before this fix.

Today the kicker registers long-lived placeholder check-runs (e.g. `Quality gate`, `JS engine integration`, `Binaries smoke gate`) on a fresh head so the PR shows "under validation" while the real gate is a dispatch-only workflow; when the cycle is superseded (new head, re-dispatch, cancellation) or ends, the placeholders are not closed. A leaked `in_progress` check is pinned to its SHA forever: GitHub computes the required-check state per name across ALL suites on the head, so ONE zombie `Quality gate` holds `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even when 58 sibling checks are green and a genuine `Quality gate: success` exists from the real CI run. The merge bot then waits `checks=pending` every tick and the PR cannot merge by any machine action — the branch is not behind, so no re-validation cycle helps.

Live instance 2026-10-17 (fa #1563, head `f3d58647`): suite 105847141092 created by the kicker push at 18:15:41Z; placeholder `Quality gate` registered 18:24:18Z (check-run id 117469671401) stayed `in_progress` 40+ minutes past its cycle; PR hard-stuck at BLOCKED; operator could not close it via REST (`POST /check-runs/{id}/completed` → 404: only the creating app may complete its own check-runs). The PR only escaped because it merged by other means. Closing that escape hatch is what makes this card load-bearing.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "close zombie check-runs by hand via API when found." Impossible in practice (creator-only restriction) and wrong in principle (see owner directive on dmtools-agents#994: manual cleanup masks the bug; the pipeline must not depend on humans GC-ing its leaks).
- **Retracted:** "the merge bot should treat in_progress checks whose workflow run completed as stale." That is the *detection* half and survives only as an input to the sweeper; the *cure* must be closing the leak at creation time plus healing what already leaked.
- **Retracted:** "wait for the next head — zombies die with their SHA." True only while the head keeps moving; a green, up-to-date, fully-validated PR with a zombie on its CURRENT head (the live instance) has no reason to move. A system where the only cure is generating new work is a leak with extra steps.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle (subject of every verb is the **check-run object**, owned by a **validation cycle** keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
cycle start (kicker/rework/operator push → new head H)
   │ registers placeholders P1..Pn on H via Checks API
   ▼
validation dispatched (dispatch-only CI, separate workflow)
   │ outcomes: success | failure | superseded (new head H') | cancelled
   ▼
finally-path [THE FIX — runs for EVERY outcome]
   ├── close P1..Pn on H with the cycle's real conclusion
   │      (success→success, failure→failure, superseded→neutral)
   └── force-complete any P_i still queued/in_progress even if the
       closing call itself failed (retry w/ backoff, then escalate)
        │
        ▼
[sweeper — self-heal pre-fix leaks]
   scan heads of open, non-dirty PRs for check-runs where
   status ∈ {queued, in_progress} AND owning workflow_run is in
   a terminal state → force-complete as neutral + log `zombie-swept`
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — leak-free creation:** for every placeholder P registered by a cycle, the cycle's termination (any path, including process kill between register and dispatch) results in P being terminal within one SM tick. There is no code path that leaves P open.
- **I2 — detection is grounded, not heuristic:** the sweeper never force-completes a check-run whose owning workflow run is still live. A live `in_progress` `Quality gate` is legitimate; only terminal-owner + open-check is a zombie.
- **I3 — required-check semantics preserved:** placeholder conclusions always mirror the cycle's real outcome (never a blanket `success`), so GitHub's required-check verdict stays truthful. `neutral` is reserved for superseded cycles — a superseded cycle carries no verdict about its head.
- **I4 — creator-only boundary respected:** all close operations run under the same app identity that created the check-runs (the cycle's own token); no cross-app completion is attempted, because GitHub rejects it (404) by design.
- **I5 — observability:** every close and every sweep action leaves a machine-log line (`check-close: <run-id> <conclusion>` / `zombie-swept: <check-run-id> head <sha>`); zombies found by the sweeper are counted in the factory state payload so operators see the leak rate, not just the fix.

## Capability surface (every cycle outcome → close obligation)

| Cycle outcome | Placeholders closed today? | Must close (this card) | Conclusion value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation success | NO (live instance: success run, open placeholder) | YES — core | `success` |
| Validation failure | unknown, assumed NO (same path) | YES — core | `failure` (keeps the PR honestly parked) |
| Superseded by newer head H' | NO | YES — core | `neutral` (no verdict carried across heads) |
| Cycle cancelled (dup dispatch, timeout) | NO | YES — core | `neutral` |
| Process died between register and dispatch | NO | YES — core (recovered by finally-on-next-tick) | `neutral` |
| Pre-fix leaked zombies on existing PRs | n/a | YES — sweeper, second tier | `neutral` + count metric |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I5 for all rows above; the finally-path lives in the SAME job that registers placeholders, so it inherits the creator token (I4 for free).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** the sweeper generalizes to a periodic (hourly) repo-wide scan for terminal-owner open checks on ANY ref, plus a factory-state metric page for the leak counter.
- **Excluded (rationale):** completing OTHER apps' check-runs (GitHub forbids; listed as *impossible*, not excluded-by-taste); changing the required-check configuration (repo settings are out of scope); converting placeholders to real job-based checks (a larger redesign — follow-up card if desired).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: the placeholder-lifecycle state machine transitions register→(success|failure|superseded|cancelled|died)→closed with the correct conclusion per the table; no transition leaves the object open. *Hook: pure state-machine UT over the five outcomes.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub API): a scripted cycle that registers 3 placeholders, then terminates with each of the five outcomes → each placeholder receives exactly one close call with the mapped conclusion; a kill between register and dispatch is recovered by the next tick's finally. *Hook: scripted API fixture with call assertions.*
- **AC3** — Zombie detection: given a check-run with `status=in_progress` whose `check_suite`/`workflow_run` is terminal, the sweeper force-completes it as `neutral` and emits the `zombie-swept` log line; a live-owner `in_progress` check is never touched. *Hook: IT with two fixtures (terminal owner vs live owner).*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox repo): reproduce the fa #1563 shape — kicker push → placeholders → superseding push → real CI green on the final head → PR mergeable WITHOUT any human or sweeper intervention, because no zombie exists on the final head. *Hook: E2E scenario named `zombie-repro-1563`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded fa #1563 timeline (suite 105847141092, check-run 117469671401) against the sweeper → the check-run ends terminal as `neutral`, the metric increments, and the PR's computed mergeability flips to the real (green) verdict. *Hook: REG fixture from the live incident; CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green…

Closes #998
### Root Cause
A placeholder check-run in `in_progress` whose owning workflow run terminated had no close path for four of the five cycle outcomes: the gh-857 in-place conclusion only mirrors a **green** verdict (and only with a probed green cover, no active head run, and an app token). Failure/superseded/cancelled/died cycles and all pre-fix leaks left the zombie pinned to its SHA — mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED forever (live fa #1563, head `f3d58647`, check-run 117469671401), and the legacy same-sha re-dispatch cannot conclude a stamp nothing will conclude.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — gh-998 lifecycle contract: `CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` + `conclusionForOutcome` (capability table), `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle` (AC1 state machine over the five outcomes; unknown outcome fails safe, double-close rejected — E1 idempotence), `zombieSweptLine` (I5 log format).
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-998 neutral sweep in the validate-pr placeholder/orphan block: terminal-owner orphans (gh-865 detector) whose cycle left no verdict are force-completed as `neutral` under the cycle's own app token (I3/I4), with the gh-857 AC2 fail-safes unchanged (no active head run; green-probe corner falls through untouched). New transport `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` emits `zombie-swept: <id> head <sha>` per close; rejections retry next tick (E2). Per-tick counter reset in `action()`.
- `js/factoryState.js` — cumulative `zombiesSwept` rides the state snapshot (I5); smAgent passes the tick count at the `buildFactoryState` call site.
- Link-less placeholders deliberately keep the gh-852 fresh-sha reset (a same-sha re-dispatch re-mints them — only a fresh head cures that pathology, gh-852 AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — 8 new tests: conclusion mapping, five-outcome lifecycle (incl. 3-placeholder multi-item), fail-safe unknown outcome, idempotent double-close rejection, `zombie-swept` log line. RED first (8 failed), GREEN after implementation.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 4 new tests: stable-shape 0, tick count, cumulative carry, malformed-carry restart.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **3590 passed, 0 failed** (clean-env re-run: 3538 passed, 0 failed — delta is env-dependent skips; new suites pass 49/49 and 145/145 standalone).

### Notes
- The creation-side finally-path for the kicker stub (Q1, shared helper) and the E2E/REG sandbox scenarios (AC4/AC5) live in the factory/kicker repos and CI — out of this repo's reach; this change is the SM-side finally-path + sweper (Q2 per-tick piggyback) + observability.
- A `neutral` close is honest but not a green verdict: the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered (I3).

# gh-998: Zombie in_progress check-run survives head change and blocks merge forever (fa #1563 live)

## Description

## Goal — leaked placeholder check-runs become unreachable, and existing zombies get swept (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **a check-run in state `in_progress`/`queued` whose owning workflow run has already terminated becomes unreachable state** — every cycle that opens placeholder check-runs closes them in a finally-path, every superseded cycle force-completes its leftovers, and a sweeper heals check-runs leaked before this fix.

Today the kicker registers long-lived placeholder check-runs (e.g. `Quality gate`, `JS engine integration`, `Binaries smoke gate`) on a fresh head so the PR shows "under validation" while the real gate is a dispatch-only workflow; when the cycle is superseded (new head, re-dispatch, cancellation) or ends, the placeholders are not closed. A leaked `in_progress` check is pinned to its SHA forever: GitHub computes the required-check state per name across ALL suites on the head, so ONE zombie `Quality gate` holds `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even when 58 sibling checks are green and a genuine `Quality gate: success` exists from the real CI run. The merge bot then waits `checks=pending` every tick and the PR cannot merge by any machine action — the branch is not behind, so no re-validation cycle helps.

Live instance 2026-10-17 (fa #1563, head `f3d58647`): suite 105847141092 created by the kicker push at 18:15:41Z; placeholder `Quality gate` registered 18:24:18Z (check-run id 117469671401) stayed `in_progress` 40+ minutes past its cycle; PR hard-stuck at BLOCKED; operator could not close it via REST (`POST /check-runs/{id}/completed` → 404: only the creating app may complete its own check-runs). The PR only escaped because it merged by other means. Closing that escape hatch is what makes this card load-bearing.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "close zombie check-runs by hand via API when found." Impossible in practice (creator-only restriction) and wrong in principle (see owner directive on dmtools-agents#994: manual cleanup masks the bug; the pipeline must not depend on humans GC-ing its leaks).
- **Retracted:** "the merge bot should treat in_progress checks whose workflow run completed as stale." That is the *detection* half and survives only as an input to the sweeper; the *cure* must be closing the leak at creation time plus healing what already leaked.
- **Retracted:** "wait for the next head — zombies die with their SHA." True only while the head keeps moving; a green, up-to-date, fully-validated PR with a zombie on its CURRENT head (the live instance) has no reason to move. A system where the only cure is generating new work is a leak with extra steps.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle (subject of every verb is the **check-run object**, owned by a **validation cycle** keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
cycle start (kicker/rework/operator push → new head H)
   │ registers placeholders P1..Pn on H via Checks API
   ▼
validation dispatched (dispatch-only CI, separate workflow)
   │ outcomes: success | failure | superseded (new head H') | cancelled
   ▼
finally-path [THE FIX — runs for EVERY outcome]
   ├── close P1..Pn on H with the cycle's real conclusion
   │      (success→success, failure→failure, superseded→neutral)
   └── force-complete any P_i still queued/in_progress even if the
       closing call itself failed (retry w/ backoff, then escalate)
        │
        ▼
[sweeper — self-heal pre-fix leaks]
   scan heads of open, non-dirty PRs for check-runs where
   status ∈ {queued, in_progress} AND owning workflow_run is in
   a terminal state → force-complete as neutral + log `zombie-swept`
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — leak-free creation:** for every placeholder P registered by a cycle, the cycle's termination (any path, including process kill between register and dispatch) results in P being terminal within one SM tick. There is no code path that leaves P open.
- **I2 — detection is grounded, not heuristic:** the sweeper never force-completes a check-run whose owning workflow run is still live. A live `in_progress` `Quality gate` is legitimate; only terminal-owner + open-check is a zombie.
- **I3 — required-check semantics preserved:** placeholder conclusions always mirror the cycle's real outcome (never a blanket `success`), so GitHub's required-check verdict stays truthful. `neutral` is reserved for superseded cycles — a superseded cycle carries no verdict about its head.
- **I4 — creator-only boundary respected:** all close operations run under the same app identity that created the check-runs (the cycle's own token); no cross-app completion is attempted, because GitHub rejects it (404) by design.
- **I5 — observability:** every close and every sweep action leaves a machine-log line (`check-close: <run-id> <conclusion>` / `zombie-swept: <check-run-id> head <sha>`); zombies found by the sweeper are counted in the factory state payload so operators see the leak rate, not just the fix.

## Capability surface (every cycle outcome → close obligation)

| Cycle outcome | Placeholders closed today? | Must close (this card) | Conclusion value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation success | NO (live instance: success run, open placeholder) | YES — core | `success` |
| Validation failure | unknown, assumed NO (same path) | YES — core | `failure` (keeps the PR honestly parked) |
| Superseded by newer head H' | NO | YES — core | `neutral` (no verdict carried across heads) |
| Cycle cancelled (dup dispatch, timeout) | NO | YES — core | `neutral` |
| Process died between register and dispatch | NO | YES — core (recovered by finally-on-next-tick) | `neutral` |
| Pre-fix leaked zombies on existing PRs | n/a | YES — sweeper, second tier | `neutral` + count metric |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I5 for all rows above; the finally-path lives in the SAME job that registers placeholders, so it inherits the creator token (I4 for free).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** the sweeper generalizes to a periodic (hourly) repo-wide scan for terminal-owner open checks on ANY ref, plus a factory-state metric page for the leak counter.
- **Excluded (rationale):** completing OTHER apps' check-runs (GitHub forbids; listed as *impossible*, not excluded-by-taste); changing the required-check configuration (repo settings are out of scope); converting placeholders to real job-based checks (a larger redesign — follow-up card if desired).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: the placeholder-lifecycle state machine transitions register→(success|failure|superseded|cancelled|died)→closed with the correct conclusion per the table; no transition leaves the object open. *Hook: pure state-machine UT over the five outcomes.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub API): a scripted cycle that registers 3 placeholders, then terminates with each of the five outcomes → each placeholder receives exactly one close call with the mapped conclusion; a kill between register and dispatch is recovered by the next tick's finally. *Hook: scripted API fixture with call assertions.*
- **AC3** — Zombie detection: given a check-run with `status=in_progress` whose `check_suite`/`workflow_run` is terminal, the sweeper force-completes it as `neutral` and emits the `zombie-swept` log line; a live-owner `in_progress` check is never touched. *Hook: IT with two fixtures (terminal owner vs live owner).*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox repo): reproduce the fa #1563 shape — kicker push → placeholders → superseding push → real CI green on the final head → PR mergeable WITHOUT any human or sweeper intervention, because no zombie exists on the final head. *Hook: E2E scenario named `zombie-repro-1563`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded fa #1563 timeline (suite 105847141092, check-run 117469671401) against the sweeper → the check-run ends terminal as `neutral`, the metric increments, and the PR's computed mergeability flips to the real (green) verdict. *Hook: REG fixture from the live incident; CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green…

Closes #998
### Root Cause
A placeholder check-run in `in_progress` whose owning workflow run terminated had no close path for four of the five cycle outcomes: the gh-857 in-place conclusion only mirrors a **green** verdict (and only with a probed green cover, no active head run, and an app token). Failure/superseded/cancelled/died cycles and all pre-fix leaks left the zombie pinned to its SHA — mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED forever (live fa #1563, head `f3d58647`, check-run 117469671401), and the legacy same-sha re-dispatch cannot conclude a stamp nothing will conclude.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — gh-998 lifecycle contract: `CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` + `conclusionForOutcome` (capability table), `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle` (AC1 state machine over the five outcomes; unknown outcome fails safe, double-close rejected — E1 idempotence), `zombieSweptLine` (I5 log format).
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-998 neutral sweep in the validate-pr placeholder/orphan block: terminal-owner orphans (gh-865 detector) whose cycle left no verdict are force-completed as `neutral` under the cycle's own app token (I3/I4), with the gh-857 AC2 fail-safes unchanged (no active head run; green-probe corner falls through untouched). New transport `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` emits `zombie-swept: <id> head <sha>` per close; rejections retry next tick (E2). Per-tick counter reset in `action()`.
- `js/factoryState.js` — cumulative `zombiesSwept` rides the state snapshot (I5); smAgent passes the tick count at the `buildFactoryState` call site.
- Link-less placeholders deliberately keep the gh-852 fresh-sha reset (a same-sha re-dispatch re-mints them — only a fresh head cures that pathology, gh-852 AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — 8 new tests: conclusion mapping, five-outcome lifecycle (incl. 3-placeholder multi-item), fail-safe unknown outcome, idempotent double-close rejection, `zombie-swept` log line. RED first (8 failed), GREEN after implementation.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 4 new tests: stable-shape 0, tick count, cumulative carry, malformed-carry restart.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **3590 passed, 0 failed** (clean-env re-run: 3538 passed, 0 failed — delta is env-dependent skips; new suites pass 49/49 and 145/145 standalone).

### Notes
- The creation-side finally-path for the kicker stub (Q1, shared helper) and the E2E/REG sandbox scenarios (AC4/AC5) live in the factory/kicker repos and CI — out of this repo's reach; this change is the SM-side finally-path + sweper (Q2 per-tick piggyback) + observability.
- A `neutral` close is honest but not a green verdict: the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered (I3).

# gh-998: Zombie in_progress check-run survives head change and blocks merge forever (fa #1563 live)

## Description

## Goal — leaked placeholder check-runs become unreachable, and existing zombies get swept (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **a check-run in state `in_progress`/`queued` whose owning workflow run has already terminated becomes unreachable state** — every cycle that opens placeholder check-runs closes them in a finally-path, every superseded cycle force-completes its leftovers, and a sweeper heals check-runs leaked before this fix.

Today the kicker registers long-lived placeholder check-runs (e.g. `Quality gate`, `JS engine integration`, `Binaries smoke gate`) on a fresh head so the PR shows "under validation" while the real gate is a dispatch-only workflow; when the cycle is superseded (new head, re-dispatch, cancellation) or ends, the placeholders are not closed. A leaked `in_progress` check is pinned to its SHA forever: GitHub computes the required-check state per name across ALL suites on the head, so ONE zombie `Quality gate` holds `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even when 58 sibling checks are green and a genuine `Quality gate: success` exists from the real CI run. The merge bot then waits `checks=pending` every tick and the PR cannot merge by any machine action — the branch is not behind, so no re-validation cycle helps.

Live instance 2026-10-17 (fa #1563, head `f3d58647`): suite 105847141092 created by the kicker push at 18:15:41Z; placeholder `Quality gate` registered 18:24:18Z (check-run id 117469671401) stayed `in_progress` 40+ minutes past its cycle; PR hard-stuck at BLOCKED; operator could not close it via REST (`POST /check-runs/{id}/completed` → 404: only the creating app may complete its own check-runs). The PR only escaped because it merged by other means. Closing that escape hatch is what makes this card load-bearing.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "close zombie check-runs by hand via API when found." Impossible in practice (creator-only restriction) and wrong in principle (see owner directive on dmtools-agents#994: manual cleanup masks the bug; the pipeline must not depend on humans GC-ing its leaks).
- **Retracted:** "the merge bot should treat in_progress checks whose workflow run completed as stale." That is the *detection* half and survives only as an input to the sweeper; the *cure* must be closing the leak at creation time plus healing what already leaked.
- **Retracted:** "wait for the next head — zombies die with their SHA." True only while the head keeps moving; a green, up-to-date, fully-validated PR with a zombie on its CURRENT head (the live instance) has no reason to move. A system where the only cure is generating new work is a leak with extra steps.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle (subject of every verb is the **check-run object**, owned by a **validation cycle** keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
cycle start (kicker/rework/operator push → new head H)
   │ registers placeholders P1..Pn on H via Checks API
   ▼
validation dispatched (dispatch-only CI, separate workflow)
   │ outcomes: success | failure | superseded (new head H') | cancelled
   ▼
finally-path [THE FIX — runs for EVERY outcome]
   ├── close P1..Pn on H with the cycle's real conclusion
   │      (success→success, failure→failure, superseded→neutral)
   └── force-complete any P_i still queued/in_progress even if the
       closing call itself failed (retry w/ backoff, then escalate)
        │
        ▼
[sweeper — self-heal pre-fix leaks]
   scan heads of open, non-dirty PRs for check-runs where
   status ∈ {queued, in_progress} AND owning workflow_run is in
   a terminal state → force-complete as neutral + log `zombie-swept`
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — leak-free creation:** for every placeholder P registered by a cycle, the cycle's termination (any path, including process kill between register and dispatch) results in P being terminal within one SM tick. There is no code path that leaves P open.
- **I2 — detection is grounded, not heuristic:** the sweeper never force-completes a check-run whose owning workflow run is still live. A live `in_progress` `Quality gate` is legitimate; only terminal-owner + open-check is a zombie.
- **I3 — required-check semantics preserved:** placeholder conclusions always mirror the cycle's real outcome (never a blanket `success`), so GitHub's required-check verdict stays truthful. `neutral` is reserved for superseded cycles — a superseded cycle carries no verdict about its head.
- **I4 — creator-only boundary respected:** all close operations run under the same app identity that created the check-runs (the cycle's own token); no cross-app completion is attempted, because GitHub rejects it (404) by design.
- **I5 — observability:** every close and every sweep action leaves a machine-log line (`check-close: <run-id> <conclusion>` / `zombie-swept: <check-run-id> head <sha>`); zombies found by the sweeper are counted in the factory state payload so operators see the leak rate, not just the fix.

## Capability surface (every cycle outcome → close obligation)

| Cycle outcome | Placeholders closed today? | Must close (this card) | Conclusion value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation success | NO (live instance: success run, open placeholder) | YES — core | `success` |
| Validation failure | unknown, assumed NO (same path) | YES — core | `failure` (keeps the PR honestly parked) |
| Superseded by newer head H' | NO | YES — core | `neutral` (no verdict carried across heads) |
| Cycle cancelled (dup dispatch, timeout) | NO | YES — core | `neutral` |
| Process died between register and dispatch | NO | YES — core (recovered by finally-on-next-tick) | `neutral` |
| Pre-fix leaked zombies on existing PRs | n/a | YES — sweeper, second tier | `neutral` + count metric |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I5 for all rows above; the finally-path lives in the SAME job that registers placeholders, so it inherits the creator token (I4 for free).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** the sweeper generalizes to a periodic (hourly) repo-wide scan for terminal-owner open checks on ANY ref, plus a factory-state metric page for the leak counter.
- **Excluded (rationale):** completing OTHER apps' check-runs (GitHub forbids; listed as *impossible*, not excluded-by-taste); changing the required-check configuration (repo settings are out of scope); converting placeholders to real job-based checks (a larger redesign — follow-up card if desired).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: the placeholder-lifecycle state machine transitions register→(success|failure|superseded|cancelled|died)→closed with the correct conclusion per the table; no transition leaves the object open. *Hook: pure state-machine UT over the five outcomes.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub API): a scripted cycle that registers 3 placeholders, then terminates with each of the five outcomes → each placeholder receives exactly one close call with the mapped conclusion; a kill between register and dispatch is recovered by the next tick's finally. *Hook: scripted API fixture with call assertions.*
- **AC3** — Zombie detection: given a check-run with `status=in_progress` whose `check_suite`/`workflow_run` is terminal, the sweeper force-completes it as `neutral` and emits the `zombie-swept` log line; a live-owner `in_progress` check is never touched. *Hook: IT with two fixtures (terminal owner vs live owner).*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox repo): reproduce the fa #1563 shape — kicker push → placeholders → superseding push → real CI green on the final head → PR mergeable WITHOUT any human or sweeper intervention, because no zombie exists on the final head. *Hook: E2E scenario named `zombie-repro-1563`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded fa #1563 timeline (suite 105847141092, check-run 117469671401) against the sweeper → the check-run ends terminal as `neutral`, the metric increments, and the PR's computed mergeability flips to the real (green) verdict. *Hook: REG fixture from the live incident; CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green…

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: AC1 lifecycle state machine has no production caller — dead code as shipped**

`CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` / `conclusionForOutcome` / `openCycle` / `closePlaceholderCycle` are exported and fully unit-tested, but nothing in production code calls them (verified: the only non-test references are the definitions and exports in this file). The actual gh-998 sweper in `js/smAgent.js` (`sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral`) hardcodes `-f conclusion=neutral` for every check-run and never consults this table — so the `success→success` and `failure→failure` rows of the capability table are unreachable in production, and a cycle that genuinely FAILED gets its zombie closed as `neutral`, not `failure` as the AC1 table mandates.

Two ways to resolve:

1. **Wire the table in** — the orphan detector's `resolveRun` already sees the owning run's `conclusion` at detection time (`orphanedRunChecks` discards it today); carry it through and map `failure`-owner orphans to `conclusion=failure` (keeping `neutral` for superseded/cancelled/died/no-conclusion), or
2. **Mark it explicitly as staged** — if this module is intended for the cross-repo kicker-side finally helper (Q1), say so at the export site with the tracking issue, so the next reader doesn't assume the finally-path is live when only the sweper is.

The PR description's "AC1 state machine over the five outcomes" reads as delivered behavior; as shipped it is tested-but-unwired. Not blocking — the neutral sweper alone does heal the live incident shape honestly (I3 holds: no required-check truth is laundered) — but the dead surface should be wired or labeled before merge.

💡 **SUGGESTION: permanently-rejected zombies retry (and warn) every tick forever — no E2 escalation path**

A rejection that can never succeed — most notably a terminal-owner check-run created by a *different* GitHub App (the gh-865 detector is not filtered to this app's own check-runs, so a third-party integration's orphaned check-run lands in `vOrphans` too) — makes GitHub 403/404 the PATCH on every tick, producing a `⚠️ zombie sweep rejected` warn per PR per tick with no progress and no alarm. Transient failures benefit from the retry, but permanent ones become log noise that masks real signal.

The ticket's E2 also asks for "a persistent failure escalates to an issue (existing alarm path) rather than silently leaking." Suggest a follow-up: bound the retries per check-run id (e.g. reject the same id N ticks in a row → post one tracker comment via the existing alarm path, then mark-and-skip it), so the sweep stays actionable instead of chatty. Fine as a separate card — does not block this PR.

## PR Description

Closes #998
### Root Cause
A placeholder check-run in `in_progress` whose owning workflow run terminated had no close path for four of the five cycle outcomes: the gh-857 in-place conclusion only mirrors a **green** verdict (and only with a probed green cover, no active head run, and an app token). Failure/superseded/cancelled/died cycles and all pre-fix leaks left the zombie pinned to its SHA — mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED forever (live fa #1563, head `f3d58647`, check-run 117469671401), and the legacy same-sha re-dispatch cannot conclude a stamp nothing will conclude.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — gh-998 lifecycle contract: `CYCLE_OUTCOME_CONCLUSIONS` + `conclusionForOutcome` (capability table), `openCycle`/`closePlaceholderCycle` (AC1 state machine over the five outcomes; unknown outcome fails safe, double-close rejected — E1 idempotence), `zombieSweptLine` (I5 log format).
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-998 neutral sweep in the validate-pr placeholder/orphan block: terminal-owner orphans (gh-865 detector) whose cycle left no verdict are force-completed as `neutral` under the cycle's own app token (I3/I4), with the gh-857 AC2 fail-safes unchanged (no active head run; green-probe corner falls through untouched). New transport `sweepZombieCheckRunsNeutral` emits `zombie-swept: <id> head <sha>` per close; rejections retry next tick (E2). Per-tick counter reset in `action()`.
- `js/factoryState.js` — cumulative `zombiesSwept` rides the state snapshot (I5); smAgent passes the tick count at the `buildFactoryState` call site.
- Link-less placeholders deliberately keep the gh-852 fresh-sha reset (a same-sha re-dispatch re-mints them — only a fresh head cures that pathology, gh-852 AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — 8 new tests: conclusion mapping, five-outcome lifecycle (incl. 3-placeholder multi-item), fail-safe unknown outcome, idempotent double-close rejection, `zombie-swept` log line. RED first (8 failed), GREEN after implementation.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 4 new tests: stable-shape 0, tick count, cumulative carry, malformed-carry restart.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **3590 passed, 0 failed** (clean-env re-run: 3538 passed, 0 failed — delta is env-dependent skips; new suites pass 49/49 and 145/145 standalone).

### Notes
- The creation-side finally-path for the kicker stub (Q1, shared helper) and the E2E/REG sandbox scenarios (AC4/AC5) live in the factory/kicker repos and CI — out of this repo's reach; this change is the SM-side finally-path + sweper (Q2 per-tick piggyback) + observability.
- A `neutral` close is honest but not a green verdict: the PR still re-validates through the existing legacy dispatch path — no required-check truth is laundered (I3).
